#ThrowbackThursday. This is one of my most treasured photos - the last one of us together as a family.

It wasn’t long after this that my sister Jacinta was killed by her partner. A few months later we lost my father in a violent and unprovoked attack relating to the custody of her young daughter. 

Obviously, I was devastated and life was extremely hard there for a while. Suddenly I was thrust into a world where I was doing police interviews, identifying weapons and attending court hearings while working out how to raise my little brother.

What I learned from that experience is that life can be unpredictable and unfair. We can’t always control what happens to us, but we can decide how we respond. 

In the months and years that followed, I found my voice. I learned to stand up for others and eventually I learned how to change our laws to be more inclusive of the people they impact. 

Since then I’ve worked across Australia and overseas to improve community safety and better enable victims of crimes to be heard.

I’m proud of what I’ve helped accomplish by working with others, including the One Punch Can Kill campaign and subsequent alcohol reforms that have saved lives.

But there’s so much more I want to achieve for our community, which is why I’ve decided to run as the Labor candidate for Cooper and why I’m asking for your support this election.

I keep getting asked this question

What do you suggest to bring chapel street back to life?

Before I go there let's discuss the past.
To answer your question, we need to look at how we got here.
The precinct has changed dramatically and so has retail over the past decade. We had boutique stores down the strip and Greville street had amazing individual stores and cafes/ bars and a great pub and a lot of national brands moved in because they did not want to miss out.
Shops were busy, the street were alive, and the night life was pumping! Incredibly the place was always SAFE.
Since then a lot has changed. Our shopping habits, population, and demographic change, and more importantly the market rental has priced many businesses, eve the strong national brands out of the area.
The look of Chapel street is tired today BUT underneath that wear and tear is the same lifeblood of vibrancy just waiting to be reborn.
Chapel street is now at a crossroads. It needs a visionary who knows how to kick start the area and bring back the WOW.
The first thing I would propose is a retail summit to bring the “best of minds” together- retailers, business owners, locals, council, and landlords.
What would need to be achieved
1. The correct retailers- engage with retailers who will bring a unique difference to chapel st - the target demographic is teenage to mid-30s
2. Landlords to invest in their property- as mentioned some street frontage is over 20 years old. Invest in your place and rent out your space. Paint the amazing fronts of these classic buildings.
3. Retailers to have web sites / click n collect / a point of difference/ offer courier service interstate and overseas
4. Customer service – what has happened to good customer service? You can spend millions on a refurb but if you get attitude from staff, you lose that customer forever.

Chronic illness, disability or carer responsibilities shouldn't be a barrier to Victorians getting tested if they have symptoms – so we’ve started a Call to Test program to arrange in-home tests. 

Access to the service will be available to individuals who have coronavirus  symptoms and meet the following criteria:

✅ people with an injury, chronic health issue, or frailty affecting mobility
✅ people with moderate to severe physical or psychosocial disability
✅ people with moderate to severe mental health or behavioural issues not otherwise classified as a psychosocial disability
✅ carers for a person with moderate to severe disability

⚠️People without symptoms may be eligible if they have been identified by the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) as being a close contact, have received direction from DHHS to be tested, and meet any of the criteria detailed above.

The Andrews Labor Government will develop a new Secure Work Pilot Scheme, to provide up to five days of sick and carer’s pay at the national minimum wage for casual or insecure workers in priority industries.

Once up and running, the two-year pilot will afford these workers sick pay when they’re unwell, and carer’s pay when they need to take time to look after someone they love. Importantly, it will mean Victorians aren’t being forced to choose between the safety of their co‑workers – and putting food on the table for their family.

We expect the pilot scheme will cover workers in select sectors with high rates of casualisation. These could include cleaners, hospitality staff, security guards, supermarket workers and aged care staff. The pilot will roll out in two phases over two years with the occupations eligible for each phase to be finalised after a consultation process that will include workers, industry and unions. 

The Victorian Budget 2020/21 will provide $5 million for consultation on the design of the pilot scheme to work through issues including documentation required to support payment applications and protections for workers who apply to access the scheme.

Art, creativity and innovation are part of the DNA of Port Phillip. We have a strong cultural heritage that brings colour and meaning to our lives and has shaped how our community sees itself. 

Creative industries account for over a third of our economic activity and are the second largest employer in Port Phillip – comprising art, culture, dance, design, fashion, film and television, media, music, theatre and photography. Architect Walter Burley Griffin believed built form should not dominate the environmental landscape, and instead "be built so that each individual can feel the whole landscape"* is theirs.

In this same vision and spirit, Griffin Ward is unique for its homes and community framed by leafy trees and spacious garden landscapes. How do we protect the special qualities of this area?

For me it starts with the planting of street trees and having a balance of indigenous, natives and exotics. We need strategic management and long term plans for our parks and gardens and the transformation of neglected places into beautiful environments.

All of this done in partnership with those that benefit most, the immediate communities who might look at an unsightly wall each day, or some rubble in a laneway, or live near a train track where the surrounding area is aesthetically unmanaged.

Some inspiration can be found in the privately owned but commons parks in Eaglemont that still contain what Walter Burley Griffin described as “Here all the children from the different houses can play together... and where they are safe from the motor traffic in the streets.”*

Now is the time for a strengthened neighbourhood character policy, a Griffin Ward overlay in planning to protect, but more importantly expand on and ensure developments respect the landscape and no longer just push it to the boundary walls.

Tired of Party Politics? Vote for a Strong Independent Voice – not a Party Puppet

With the opinion polls for the October 31st state election indicating a hung parliament is possible, Independent MPs on the cross-bench may well hold the balance of power in the next parliament. Now is the time to take advantage of this situation – Oodgeroo should not continue to miss out on State funding because the local MP is a member of the opposition. An independent can deliver better deals, and work with whichever party is in government. 

Support of one or members of the cross-bench has been necessary to allow government to form – a minority government – previously in the QLD parliament. One of the most well-known recent ‘king makers’ in the QLD parliament was Peter Wellington, Independent MP for Nicklin on the Sunshine Coast from 1998 to 2017. Mr Wellington rose to the position of Speaker of the House from 2015 through to his retirement in 2017, one of the most senior positions in government.

Regardless of whether the cross-bench holds the balance of power, an independent can achieve significantly more success than an MP in opposition – consider, for example, the lack of progress over the last 6 years while the local Oodgeroo MP has been in opposition. An independent is never ‘in opposition’ and as a member of the cross-bench will be able to negotiate with whichever party is in power to achieve better outcomes for the community.

The role of an independent Member of Parliament is to represent their electorate and achieve the best results for their constituents. Independents can vote according to the wishes of their electorate – MPs who belong to political parties are expected to follow the party line on most votes, not their constituents. Even where a vote of conscience is held – which in theory allows a party MP to vote according to their beliefs - penalty’s such as future deselection could be a risk if the MP does not vote in accordance with the party policy. Because of this, unless an MP is planning to retire at the next election, even for a vote of conscience it is common for party MPs to vote in accordance with the party policy.

Independents play an important role in parliament, including preparing private member bills for debate in the house, voting on legislation and proposing bills with other members of the cross-bench. Independent MPs also take other roles within parliament, including membership of parliamentary committees that develop and review legislation, through to senior positions within government.

Sandy Bolton, Independent MP for Noosa, was elected to the Queensland State Parliament in 2017 (photograph shows Sandy and I at QLD State Parliament).

I recently met with Sandy at State Parliament and was inspired by the positive and community focused approach she adopts. During a previous meeting Sandy explained how the work of an Independent MP is not always high profile but is, nevertheless, important. An Independent MP provides true representation for their community and is able to adopt a detached and a non-partisan view on the policies before parliament.  Sandy also explained that the support she receives from the Noosa community and her ability to represent that community in Parliament is fundamental to her success as an MP.

Follow the example of Noosa – vote for an Independent to provide better outcomes for our Redlands community. 

Let’s aim to be more like Noosa – not the Gold Coast!

The NSL needs your help!

The Census question on religion is loaded but the Australian Bureau of Statistics has rejected our arguments that this is so. We want to gather evidence that this is the case via national, independent polling which asks two different questions -- the ABS's question and a non-leading alternative. We are confident of finding a statistically significant bias, but we need proof.

This evidence will be critical in convincing the ABS to change their loaded question, and will add enormously to combined campaigning being carried out by pro-secular groups in the lead-up to the Census on 10th August.

Have you ever been scammed? I have, I have been tried twice recently. It made me far more aware of the problem and the need for everyone of us to stay alert.

Scammers are becoming more sophisticated in the way they try and steal our money or personal details.

More recently scammers have taken advantage of new technologies, using social media apps and emails to contact potential victims.

Just last week I was sent an email that seemed to be from my bank.

But when I looked at it more closely, it was someone trying to fool me into giving them my bank account details.I know I'm not the only one to receive these fake emails.

Australians lost more than $634 million to scams last year. There were more than 350,000 cases, the real figure is probably much higher as many people don’t report being ripped off.

There’ve been reports of more than 4000 scams mentioning Coronavirus, robbing Australians of $3 million at a time when every single dollar counts.

So please be careful, stay on your guard and if you think you’re being scammed ask a friend, a family member or contact the business directly. Don’t be embarrassed or too scared to ask for help.

You can always say no, hang up the phone or delete an email. It doesn’t matter if you’ve said yes previously. You don’t owe the scammer anything.

Importantly, if you think your bank account details have been compromised, notify your financial institution immediately.

You can report a scam by contacting the ACCC on 1300 302 502.

As always, my office is here to help if we can. Please take care.

That’s just as I see it.
ad_creative_link_title: Just As I See It: Scams

Fitzroy Street is struggling.

Since the start of the pandemic, we have seen Acland Street and other local shops follow suit. 

This isn’t right and locals know it. 

Both streets have been in trouble for years before COVID (especially Fitzroy) and I think this should be acknowledged. 

There is no magic fix.

Our streets face a complex set of issues that will not be fixed overnight.

We must however work hard to tackle each and every issue.

Every resident, every trader and every visitor has the right to feel – and be – safe while out in our community.

That extends to those most vulnerable – always.

I want to see a renewed partnership between Council, the State Government, Victoria Police and local service providers.

We each hold different pieces to the puzzle. 

Only working together can we assist those who need help.

I will never support policies that push people out of our community.

Nor will I stand by and accept violence and verbal intimidation. 

Council and other levels of government must invest in long-term solutions – more permanent community housing, more integrated support services, and drug trafficking surveillance. 

A Band-Aid approach will not work.  

As we emerge from lockdown, we must act fast to revive our shopping strips in a COVID-safe way.

The anticipated work on Fitzroy Street with Renew Australia is a good way to do this.

We can create reasons for locals and visitors to return to our local shopping strips.

Outdoor dining, street-based live music performances, pop-up art and retail in vacant shops and special events can all play their part.

Activity feeds activity.  

The Victorian Pride Centre will help on Fitzroy Street too.

I am not going to promise I will fix these issues day one, week one or year one.

But I am in this for the long haul.

I do not have all the answers but know together significant improvements can be made. 

If current approaches do not work, we must accept, learn and change.

Council must lead this critical work.  If elected, I’ll make sure they do.

bi) they are a construction worker attending a construction site immediately outside the border zone; and

bii) they travel by private vehicle to and from the construction site without exiting the vehicle and do not leave the confines of the construction site; and

c) must not enter Queensland if the resident had travelled in a COVID-19 hotspot outside the border zone within the 14 days prior to entering Queensland.

a) permitted to enter and remain in the border zone within New South Wales; and
b) must quarantine in accordance with the requirements in Part 3 and Schedule 2 if the resident enters a COVID-19 hotspot outside the border zone.

Part 3—QUARANTINE

18. Any person who has not been to a COVID-19 hotspot in the preceding 14 days, or is not a confirmed case of COVID-19, may enter Queensland.
19. A person who enters Queensland must quarantine if in the 14 days prior to entering Queensland:
a) the person has been overseas; or
b) the person has had contact with a person who is a confirmed case of COVID-19; or
c) the person has been in a COVID-19 hotspot and is permitted to enter under Part 2; or
d) the person has been a cleared case of COVID-19 who has been given an exemption to enter Queensland by the Chief Health Officer under paragraph 21; or
e) the person has had symptoms consistent with COVID-19; or
f) the person is a border zone resident who is a Queensland resident who traveled outside the border zone in New South Wales.
20. A person who is required to quarantine under this direction:
a) must comply with the requirements for quarantine, if any, in Schedule 2; and
b) will be quarantined for a further period of 10 days from the end of the quarantine period in Schedule 2 if the person is not tested for COVID-19 when requested to do so by an emergency officer (public health); and
c) Chapter 8, Part 7AA of the Public Health Act 2005 applies to a person required to quarantine under this Direction.

Part 4—OTHER MATTERS

21. The Chief Health Officer may give a person or class of persons an exemption:

22. An emergency officer (public health) can require any person to quarantine if the emergency officer believes the direction is reasonably necessary to assist in containing, or to respond to, the spread of COVID-19 within the community.
23. Only the Chief Health Officer or the Deputy Chief Health Officer can exempt a person from entering quarantine as required under this Direction.

Mr Whippy - The legend, The Myth

Meet Peter Giunta aka “ Mr Whippy”
 
I recently had the pleasure of interviewing the man behind many joyous faces and wonderful childhood memories in Maribyrnong and he has been serving joy in cups and cones for over 40 years!
 
My first recollection of Pete is as a little kid studying in West Footscray Primary School and chasing him down, after school, following his whippy jingle, and about 8 other kids racing after him with me. There was no greater joy than hearing that sweet melodious sound, other than waiting for Captain Planet and The Chipmunks cartoons to play on television. 
 
Peter was born in an underdeveloped part of Sicily, Italy, and migrated as a 13 year old boy to Melbourne for a better life and opportunities.
 
He attended 2 years of high school and dropped out to work in factories and work odd jobs to meet ends.
 
At the age of 23 he found love and married the woman of his dreams. The couple went to Sydney, NSW, for their honeymoon.
This is where Pete heard the first whippy jingle of his life and instantly fell in love with the concept.
 
He came back to Melbourne and immediately set his heart on purchasing a Whippy Truck, but unfortunately he didn’t receive a lot of support from family or friends as the concept of Soft Serve on wheels wasn’t as trendy back then.
They even called him a looney for spending his life’s fortune on his first truck, which cost him $7,000 to setup.
 
Pete went into flashback as I asked him how it was at beginning of his career.
“There was no McDonald’s, Hungry Jacks or as many ice cream freezers. The only way to get a soft serve was to come running out of your house when Mr Whippy came around.”
He recalls buying soft serves himself for threepence!
 
Time flew by and by the turn of the 21st Century franchises such as McDonald’s killed off many whippy vans: they could simply not survive against a 20c soft serve cone.
“Even the fast food businesses were ok to deal with but what gave me real competition was technology”.
As the digital age increased, with the rise of computers, game consoles and phones, Pete witnessed a drastic decline in kids coming outside or even playing outside compared to his earlier years in business.
 
But Pete persisted and continued doing what he found his life’s passion in, serving ice cream and providing much needed joy to kids and adults alike that came out for it.
 
After separating from his partner (due to some every emotional circumstances) and going through a recent breakdown, Pete contacted me as I had engaged him several times a year in all the festivals I arranged over the last 4 years. He was my ‘go to’ man for every event I’ve organised where Ice cream was required.
 
He asked me what the future of events and festivals would be, as they were the largest source of his income.
He had been pretty much out of work since the original lock down in March this year and even contemplated putting his boots up as things seemed to be getting more dire.
 
I quickly realised that selling soft serve, Pete couldn’t register himself on the new popular delivery platforms such as Menulog, Uber Eats etc.
I tried to compile a list of streets for him after taking a poll from my local Facebook community pages, as to where Pete could visit, as he had no idea where the kids were.
 
That backfired as Pete couldn’t use navigation systems, and stopping to read a Melways that I offered him (yes I found a Melways stashed in my Dad’s garage pile of treasure(or trash), wasn’t an option for his aging eyes.
 
Only one way left for me! Get the Mr Whippy Tracker out! 
I became his assistant one fine weekend and turned on live GPS tracking on an app on my phone wereby residents could track where he was. It was novelty and a lot of fun for the kids, tracking “The Mr Whippy”.
 
This allowed me to show Pete the streets with the most kids so he could maximize his sales for the day, especially as the warmer season kicks in. He now has a nice route setup and he makes his way to those streets, once again providing joy, fun and soft serve for kids of all ages!
 
Next time you’re outside the house and hear the melodious jingle, be sure to make a run for Mr Whippy!

West Footscray (or beyond) Pop Up Art Displays
 
Covid-19 has taught us all a new way to look at life in its entirety. A year ago we would not have imagined what most of us are going through now.
 
But we’ve done our best to cope with the changing restrictions and hopefully the near future brings a stronger community connection where we all look out for each other.
 
I’ve experienced these positive changes throughout the entire pandemic, since I started delivering free groceries for the elderly and disabled. Then followed free groceries and cooked meals for temporary residents and students, and meals and supplies for the residents in the tower lockdowns.
 
People came forward to help me every step of the way. Some residents identified neighbours who were in need, a small independent supermarket, IGA, assisted me financially to help with groceries, and the community of West Footscray donated money to fund my grocery drop off to the tower lockdowns. It’s proof that a pandemic can bring out the worst but also the best in people.

Today I want to share my vision of utilising the empty spaces that have been abandoned for a while, and possibly more to come due to the closures as a result of Covid.
 
The West Footscray pop up art display is not entirely a new concept. In 2018 I sanctioned a programme through the Traders Association, whereby we used a vacant shop as a temporary pop up shop where one side sold pre-loved clothing and the other side plants. It was a success and the community enjoyed and supported it.
 
I am proposing to use the vacant shops along Barkly Street, West Footscray, for shopfront art displays and temporary galleries including plants and flower galleries.
I have already been in talks with local, community-minded artists and would like to display and share their talent with the rest of the community.

As an example, a couple of our local  talents propose using the disused shopfronts for an ever- evolving art installation featuring live plants and basket weaving and dying materials.

Covid-19 saw the closure of many businesses along the strip, which makes the entire strip and area look rundown. These empty shops are more prone to graffiti tagging and continue to bring the look of the entire area down. The future looks bleak for many new aspiring businesses, as they are wary of restrictions coming back again and unsure what the future holds.
 
I think our council is in a position to support such programmes, which help the empty shops as well as local talent, and encourage the community to come out and admire the art. We could extend this programme to entire Maribyrnong area with the right backing from council.
 
The attached photos are actual samples of local artists’ work that we could showcase through the empty shopfront window displays.

Watch out for these in the near future and if we can get council support we can extend this program to the entire city.

I bring more than two decades of experience as a training and organisation development senior manager, in Australia and internationally. Community engagement, advice from experts, creativity, transparency and teamwork is what I believe the new team of Councillors need to harness to achieve the community’s collective vision for a revitalised Frankston.

Being Passionate: Bringing out the best in people is what I love to do. My upbringing taught me to make good use of the things I’d worked hard for, so I’m passionate about making the best use of resources too. 

Sharing Experience: As a leader in commercial and not-for-profit organisations. I value the importance of:
• listening to really hear what’s being said
• accountability and ownership for delivering agreed outcomes
• integrity and honesty
• healthy debate to challenge the status quo to solve real problems and innovate
I hold a Master of Business in Leadership and bring hands on experience and knowledge of sectors including disability, hospitality, retail, social housing, tourism, financial services, manufacturing and IT.

Contributing to the community in which I live is important to me. Frankston is my home and my community now.

I have worked and volunteered in Tasmania’s health and community services sector for 17 years and have seen first hand the damage that cuts to these services can do to individuals, families and communities.
I’m a mum, with two school age daughters. For six years I was a single mum, walking the tightrope of work, study and parenting and struggling to make ends meet. I relied on people during that time more than I ever thought I would have to. I changed jobs. I could not afford my own house, so we moved four times and relied heavily on my mum. Update – SHELLEY BEACH PARK OPTION 2 ADOPTED BY COUNCIL
Lastnight at Council the debate for Shelley Beach Park took place. There were 9 deputations representing all ages and interest groups, some of which were incredibly impressive. I thank all of those who took the time out of their busy lives to come to the meeting, the public gallery was packed!

Councillor Ben Kunze and I moved an amendment for Option 3 to be considered. My reasoning during debate is because I genuinely believe from the data provided and my interactions with the Community it was what the Community wanted. I also stated I personally was not fussed about whether there was a café or not, however my personal opinions and feelings should not come into consideration when making decisions on behalf of the Community. This is something I strongly believe in and will continue to demonstrate whilst I sit on this Council.

This amendment was not supported by the entire Council with some stating it was their belief that statistics and data could be interpreted in any way and so they voted against option 3. 

We came very close to not having any of the options endorsed, which in my mind, would have been catastrophic for this Community. Luckily, we were able to convince Council that Option 2 was the best option for the Community considering Option 3 was not supported.

I am sorry to those who feel let down by the decision. I am hopeful we can now all move on and share the Shelley Foreshore as one welcoming and friendly Community. My Children are incredibly excited for a new playground as I'm sure so too are yours.

CSNSW IS GETTING A BLUE LEASE ON LIFE 

Corrective Services NSW has installed its first ‘blue tree’ to raise awareness about mental health issues and suicide prevention.

The tree was commissioned at the Brush Farm Corrective Services Academy at Eastwood in Sydney's north-west as part of the Blue Tree Project.

The scheme started in Western Australia in 2018 when a young woman painted a dead-tree blue, in memory of her brother, who took his life. 

Since then, more than 600 trees have been painted blue across Australia, New Zealand, the UK, USA and Europe.

Hunter Correctional Centre-based manager Vicki Rivett lost her son Luke Watson last year and has inspired CSNSW to take part in the project. 

Hunter inmates are now building a blue metal tree at the centre in Luke's memory.

"I can't tell you how appreciative I am with everyone's support and interest in this project," Vicki said.

CSNSW is aiming is to have 50 blue trees across our sites by World Suicide Prevention day on 10 September.

To learn more, visit bluetreeproject.com.au

The Australianism 'Clayton’s' arose from an ad campaign in the 1970s and 80s for a non-alcoholic drink, sold in a bottle that resembled a bottle of spirits. The ad was set in a bar and featured actor Jack Thompson.
Something about the line ‘the drink you’re having when you’re not having a drink’ struck a chord with the Australian public. Clayton’s was a word waiting to happen, and it came to mean ‘something that is largely illusory or exists in name only; a poor substitute or imitation’.

STAGE 4 RESTRICTIONS STARTED AT 6PM 2 August: The CHO and Premier have announced the following under Stage 4 for Metro Melbourne. The following addresses how we move around, the Premier will tomorrow announce further restrictions on the way we work. 

🚨 STATE OF DISASTER ANNOUNCED FOR 4 WEEK MIN🚨 

⚠️🗣PLEASE SHARE TO HELP ME KEEP OUR COMMUNITY INFORMED⚠️🗣

🚨 CURFEW 🚨
Every night from 8pm to 5am you will not be able to leave the house (exempt for permitted work, care or caregiving, medical and compassionate reasons)

NEW RULES below will run until September 13 ⏰

The reasons to leave your home MUST BE WITHIN 5km with some exemptions as below. 🏠

1️⃣ Shopping for food or other essential items (one person per household, once a day)

2️⃣ To provide care giving, for compassionate reasons or to seek medical treatment (If you need to travel further than 5km of your house for medical care and caregiving, you will be permitted to do so).

3️⃣ For exercise (outdoor exercise only FOR ONE hour a day with only one other person including those in your household);

4️⃣ Work or study, only if you are in a permitted work or study industry

⚠️ Intimate partner visits allowed outside of 5kms.

⚠️ Movement between metropolitan Melbourne and regional Victoria will not be permitted for exercise. Travel between regional Victoria and metropolitan Melbourne will be possible for shopping for food and essential supplies, so long as you abide by the 5km limit. Travel will also be possible for medical care and caregiving, and work and education only where necessary.

CARE AND COMPASSIONATE GROUNDS INCLUDE:
⚠️CARE AND COMPASSIONATE REASONS INCLUDE:
• care for others, for example to drop food and personal care items to dependents or those who are self-isolated or who rely on your assistance

• care arrangements for children, including shared custody arrangements and the need to move kids from one parent to another in accordance with a court order or informal arrangements.

This would also include care arrangements for children that are required to enable work for permitted workers.

⚠️ You can take a pet to the vet.

EDUCATION 👦🧒
⚠️ Year 11 & 12 students across Victoria will return to remote and flexible learning on WEDNESDAY. All classes to remote learning on Wednesday.
⚠️ As normal per on Monday, but a pupil free day on Tuesday.
Exemptions for vulnerable kids, kids of permitted workers, specialist schools in Metro Melbourne for vulnerable students and children of permitted workers.
⚠️ NO CHANGES to exam, certificate and ATAR dates

CHILDCARE 👶👧
❌ Closed later in the week, except for vulnerable kids and those of permitted workers. These rules will also apply for our early childhood sector and more will be announced soon.

TRAVEL
⚠️ Travel in a vehicle with people outside your household not permitted, with some exemptions. 

SHOPPING 🛍 🛒
⚠️ One person can go out for shopping per household. Within 5kms (or at the nearest available supermarket) and only once a day. Allowances for assisting elderly and caregiving. .

EXERCISE 🏃‍♀️ 🏃‍♂️ 🚴‍♀️
⚠️ Maximum of one hour a day within 5km of home, with one other person. NOT PERMITTED TO TRAVEL TO REGIONAL VIC TO EXERCISE. (An exception is allowed for individuals with dependents to also be present where they cannot be left alone).
⚠️ Fishing, golfing, boating, tennis, surfing and drive range shooting not allowed

RESTAURANTS & CAFES ☕️ 🥘
⚠️ Takeaways and home deliveries are still allowed, subject to conditions.

PUBLIC GATHERINGS
❌ Weddings will no longer be permitted from Thursday
⚠️ Only 10 mourners can leave Melbourne for regional funerals.
❌ Organised sport is banned.

⚠️Frequently Asked Questions: 

Q - How do I report breaches of restrictions / breaking the law?
A - Via the Police Assistance Line on 131 444

Q - I live in metropolitan Melbourne and am meant to move house next week. Can I still move?
A - Yes. You are still able to move house, but the curfew hours still apply. You should also take extra steps to stay safe including wearing a face covering.

Q - Where is my place of residence?
A - The easiest way to think about it is, where you slept last night, is where you need to stay for the next six weeks. No moving between residences and a week each at of your mate’s places.
As of tonight, people in metropolitan Melbourne will be required to remain wherever they stayed last night. There will be exemptions for some situations, including work and medical care and compassionate reasons.
Individuals will be required to demonstrate proof of their place of residence. This could be provided with documents including a driver’s licence, rates notice, utility bill.

Q - Can I leave metropolitan Melbourne to go to a funeral?
A - Yes, you may leave metropolitan Melbourne to attend a funeral. The restrictions of 10 mourners attending a funeral will apply in regional Victoria.

Q - What are ‘essential supplies’?
A - Essential supplies include things like food, groceries, pharmaceutical or medical supplies, essential clothing, urgent supplies for household or mechanical repairs.

Q - What does ‘medical, care or compassionate needs’ mean?
A - This means that you may leave your house for medical reasons including to see a doctor, mental health treatment, an allied health professional, Alcohol and Drug support, or go to the pharmacy, but only if you absolutely need to.

Q - Can I provide care/support to a friend or relative who is in self-isolation?
A - Care reasons to leave the home include essential excursions to care for others, for example to drop food and personal care items to dependents or those who are self-isolated or rely on your assistance. ‘Medical, care or compassionate needs’ includes mental health needs.

Q - Can I visit my friend’s house? (This one is obvious, but will mention anyhow)
A - No. Visitors to the home are not permitted state-wide. Exceptions will apply for medical and care reasons, and emergencies. Partners can visit one another.

⚠️ Message from the Premier: 

'I know how much Victorians want to go back to some semblance of normal – or at least “COVID normal”.

They want to be able to get a beer with their mates. To drop round and see mum. And they definitely want an end to these daily updates and their grim new milestones. 

Our health experts tell us the measures we’ve introduced are working. But too slowly. 

The current rate of community transmission – mystery cases that cannot be traced back to work or home – is far too high.

As they tell us, based on the current numbers, cases might begin to drop off not in days or weeks – but in months. Months more of lockdown restrictions. Months more of 300, 400, 500 cases a day.

More Victorians in hospital beds. More Victorians hooked up to machines just to breathe.

And more Victorians – more grandparents, parents, sons, daughters, partners and loved ones – choked to death by an invisible enemy.
That’s not something I’m willing to accept. I don’t think it’s something any of us are willing to accept.

We must do more. We must go harder. It’s the only way we’ll get to the other side of this. 

I know Victorians are with me when I say, too many people are not taking this seriously. And too many people not taking this seriously means that too many other people are having to plan funerals for those they love'.

For the full statement on this and Regional Victoria go here - https://www.premier.vic.gov.au/statement-changes-melbournes-restrictions

I know how difficult a day this is for all of us in our community and Victoria. it has been an extremely hard few months for our community and today is even harder. 

There is no denying it, it is going to be a difficult few weeks ahead, we will all face our challenges and many in our community more so than others. 

Please all, look after yourself, stay home, stay safe, practice good hand hygiene, avoid touching your face and if you have got symptoms, however mild - get tested.

Please continue to help out those who need it most. And, don't be afraid to ask for help yourself if you need it.

I am here as always to help in any way I may be able to, you can get me on email jackson.taylor@parliament.vic.gov.au or calling 9738 0577. 

I will do my absolute best to get back to you as quick as I can and to keep you updated along the way. 

Be kind to one another, we need it now more than ever. 

Jackson

New housing in Arundel for older women at risk of homelessness officially opened 🙌

Rendu House, run by Vinnies QLD, opened last June but (like a lot of things in 2020) delayed their celebration until today.

It includes six refurbished units which have all been tenanted already with women over 65. 

Their first tenant was Elizabeth*. To say she’s been through hell is an understatement. 

Her first son accidentally electrocuted himself in front of her. She was also injured in the accident and still suffers from ongoing nerve damage. 

Her daughter was later murdered in a tragic case of mistaken identity. 

Her other son was diagnosed with bowel cancer. He survived it but when he moved into her house with his partner while rebuilding his life, they kicked Elizabeth out of her home because of a conflict with his partner. 

Elizabeth found herself homeless. Vinnies has helped her get through each day. This housing is an essential part of that. 

This building used to be an under-utilised administrative block. 

Vinnies has taken the $550,000 raised through the Vinnies CEO Sleepout on the Gold Coast to refurbish the units into this purpose-built accommodation. 

I’ve been proud to take part in these sleepouts over the last few years as your MP so I’m stoked to see the funds it’s raised being spent on an incredible project like this in our area 👏

The updates and key information of the Directions are as follow but please be aware that more detail is contained within each direction.

Public Activities
➡️ The total number of people present at a place must not exceed 1 person per 4 square metres.

➡️Gatherings
▪️Onsite purchase and consumption of food and beverages- 100 people max & no more than 10 people at each table. 
▪️Funeral- 50 people max 
▪️Weddings- 150 people max & registration of all guests with SA Health
▪️Religious Ceremonies- 100 people max 
▪️Private gatherings- 50 people max 
▪️Private residence- 10 people max (unless more than 10 people permanently live at the house then they are permitted to stay)
▪️Caravan park-  maximum of 10 people per site.
▪️All other holiday accommodation- maximum number of people permitted to sleep the premises up to 10 people max.

➡️ Food and beverages must be consumed while seated. 

➡️ Gyms, recreation centres, trampoline and play cafes are to close. 

➡️ Outdoor fitness and recreation activities such as boot camps are still permitted. 

➡️ Swimming for fitness or rehabilitation purposes at swimming pools is still permitted.

➡️ Entertainment venues (including museums, cinemas, zoos, etc., see direction for more).

➡️ Personal Care (beauty salons, tattoo parlours, day spas, etc., see direction for more) must ensure employees wear PPE when providing services. 

Residential Aged Care
➡️ A person cannot provide care at one care facility within 14 days of providing care at a different facility.

➡️ A person providing personal care, nursing, health, medical or allied health services to residents must wear appropriate personal protective equipment, if they are within 1.5 metres from the resident, whilst providing care. 

➡️ Care and support visits made to residents of an aged care facility are now restricted to 2 people per day.  

Further COVID-19 Advice
The SA Government has released updated COVID-19 advice due to the Parafield cluster. Please note the following are recommended but do not form part of a formal directive at this point in time.

➡️ South Australian residents should work from home where possible.

➡️ Vulnerable people are advised to stay at home and avoid having visitors at the moment.

➡️ Unnecessary travel is discouraged. 

➡️ South Australian residents should wear a mask when physical distancing of 1.5m cannot be observed, e.g. on public transport. 
.

3. When indigenous leaders are calling for change and refer to the date as marking "the start of a war" - there is a problem.
https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/jan/26/australians-turn-out-in-large-numbers-for-invasion-day-rallies-despite-covid-restrictions

4. Also, when tens of thousands march all across the country and call it "invasion day" - there is a problem.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3kOuYAxfsDw

5. Finally, please see how Heather Holmes-Ross - Mayor of City of Mitcham put this problem to the media  
https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/messenger/east-hills/mitcham-council-backs-mayors-push-to-join-change-the-date-movement/news-story/cf67b937f4cfd9f7c95efefbad83780d

“At the moment, it’s our nation’s national day and we’re happy to celebrate our nation,” Dr Holmes-Ross said. “We would rather do it on a different date.”

She said it was “absolutely” the council’s responsibility to advocate for the date to be changed because “we are the closest level of government to the people, so if there are thoughts within the community … it’s our job to pass them on to different levels of government that might not be as in touch with the general public”. 

She said she believed most people felt Australia Day was “marred by its historical context”.

So - that's my evidence for why there is a problem with the date. Please note it's evidence primarily from the mouths and actions of Aboriginal people. 

If you don't agree that's your choice, but please reflect on these questions I am asking people who oppose our collective decision.

1. Why are you so attached to the existing date for Australia Day given the obvious views of Aboriginal people? 

2. Do you appreciate that we could celebrate Australia Day on a different date quite easily, at no additional cost ?

3. Would you be ok with any of these other dates ?
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_Day#Suggested_alternative_dates

Please feel free to come give us your views in person next Tuesday at 7PM with a deputation to Council. We don't anticipate there will be queue.

ps it's on Wikipedia now.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_Day#cite_ref-73
On 23 February 2021, the City of Mitcham became the first in SA to vote to officially oppose the date of Australia Day. Mayor Dr Holmes-Ross said she felt “comfortable with the council holding events on Australia Day, but I don’t feel comfortable with the date of Australia Day”.[73]

As an introduction, I was born in Sydney, to migrant parents from non English speaking backgrounds. My connections to Gympie started when my father moved here in 1980. 

I grew up with my mother, partially in Housing Commission. My first job was as a paper boy at the local railway station at 5am and again after school doing the local run, then working for a large retailer in the Auto section till I finished High School.

Finishing up travelling through Europe for many years after High School, I completed military service in Belgium while serving with NATO forces as a truck driver in what was then West Germany. I retain connections to Belgium from my army days and value the history we share, our soldiers having fought together in Flanders Fields during World War 1.  

Returning to Australia, I joined the ADF and was in RMC Duntroon however was medically discharged.

For the last 17 years I have worked in high end customer service roles for Australian owned travel companies, following on from experiences gained in travel services in Berlin and disability travel services in New York and Geelong.

As an Independent, I represent you, not a party.

Our community deserves better than to be taken for granted or ignored by political parties. I would consider it a great honour to serve and represent the wishes of our community. I aim to fight for the best possible outcomes for Gympie and welcome your thoughts and feedback as we go on this journey together. 

Thanks.

COMMUNITY UPDATE - DAWN FRASER BATHS RESTORATION 
 
I am writing to update you about the restoration of Dawn Fraser Baths.

At the last election, I promised to save Dawn Fraser Baths and thankfully the heritage restoration of Australia’s oldest and greatest harbourside pool has now been completed.

The truth is that there have been years of neglect and underinvestment in repairing the pool. Not a single dollar was invested in upgrading the pool in the years when Jamie Parker and the Greens Party controlled Leichhardt Council.

That’s why I have fought so hard to deliver this once-in-a-generation restoration, which has secured the future of our famous Baths for years to come.

In 2018, after Balmain Ward Councillors attempted to cut the budget for the upgrade of the pool, I convened a Save Dawny’s Rally at the Baths at which hundreds of locals attended to send a message to Council that the doors of our beloved pool must remain open.

Thanks to you Dawny’s has been saved.

Unfortunately, Council officers have now notified Councillors that the reopening of the Baths has been delayed due to complications with the installation of fire safety pumps.

I learned how to swim in Dawn Fraser Baths. I know just how special this place is and the how integral it is to life in our community and much local people are looking forward to the reopening. 

I am very frustrated that commitments made by the Council to complete the heritage restoration in time for the 2020/21 summer season have not been met.

The advice that Councillors and the community have received from the Council executive about the timing of the reopening has changed continuously and that is not good enough.

I am determined that our community get to enjoy using Dawn Fraser Baths this year. 

That’s why I have tabled a mayoral minute for the first Council meeting of the year proposing that the Baths be kept open for all of 2021 and that a range of exercise and recreation programs be offered to the community there throughout the year.

A date for opening has not yet been set due to the challenges with supplying water to fire hydrants and sprinklers for emergency services. Engineers are finalising plans for the water pipe which is being installed down a steep bank while protecting significant trees.

Visit www.innerwest.nsw.gov.au/dawn-fraser-baths-upgrade for more details.

While other councils across Sydney are closing public pools, in the Inner West, we are taking the opposite approach.

In this term we have rebuilt the Ashfield Aquatic Centre (opened in October), restored Dawn Fraser Baths and dedicated a further $5.3 million to improve Leichhardt Park Aquatic Centre.

I will keep you updated as soon as I receive more information about the opening date.

It’s International Women’s Day but I find little to celebrate.  
I am so very weary. So tired of fighting and failing. So tired of waiting for ‘good men’ to take action when the system that supports them continues to fail us.
I’m tired of waiting. 
Because it’s 2021 and we still haven’t fixed the pay gap despite legislating for equal pay in 1969. 
Because women are still woefully under represented in leadership positions in both the private and public sector despite evidence of the economic and social value of women on boards.
 Because women are still not safe on the streets, in their homes or in their workplaces.
Because women are more likely to be hurt by someone they should be able to trust. 
Because women are not believed when they report crime against them.
Because I’m waiting for ‘good men’ to take action and call out rape culture.
This last few weeks has reinforced why women don’t report sexual assault.  
Because ‘he said, she said’.
Because ‘he’ deserves a fair legal process.
Because ‘she’ was drunk.
Because ‘his’ mental stress demonstrates his innocence and ‘hers’ demonstrates her confusion and lack of credibility.
Because ‘we should believe’ only applies to some.

Why don’t women report?   Because of this.

Women celebrate IWD to mark our progress and plan future action.  We should not still have so much to do.

Where are all the good men now?  Those that rally only when women organise them?

Those that stand with women when it suits but are silent if it’s a mate or a work colleagues - or worse - use their positions to deny her voice.

I’m tired. 

Happy IWD.  Here is an excellent article from Jane Gilmore about women and the reporting of rape. It contains a link to an ABC report on police responses across Australia.

NETBALL AND BASKETBALL IN EAST WARD. IGNORE THE EMAIL. DON’T VOTE GREENS.

I am an East Ward resident. I have a daughter who was about to start Net Set Go before COVID struck. My wife plays the occasional game of social netball, and I play social mixed netball and social indoor soccer. I have played at Orrong Romanis Reserve and also outside the municipality. I have coached kids sport.

I do not support building netball courts and Percy Treyvaud reserve. 

The residents, who know this area well, know that this is the wrong venue. I think based on discussions that I have had, that deep down, Prahran netballers and all Stonnington councillors know this is the wrong venue too.

East Malvern residents have also nominated a solution for the right venue. It is the site of the old East Malvern RSL. This is a better site. It is next to existing football ovals. It is more central to Stonnington. It is a place that parents will be able to bring their children to at the same time, whilst their children participate in various sports, both football and netball.

It is not next door to Melbourne’s busiest shopping centre. It will not result in 100 year old trees getting chopped down to be replaced with saplings. It will not result in us losing some of our precious open green space.

In redeveloping this site and building these netball courts we can also give a much needed cash injection to our local RSL. We can give them a first class facility to meet and a local venue where we can appropriately commemorate and recognise those who served our country in its hours of need.

Moving the netball courts from Percy Treyvaud to the site of the East Malvern RSL would be a win for East Ward, a win for netball, a win for the RSL and a win for residents.

On 29 September 2020 I wrote to a representative of the Prahran Netball Association with this proposal. The Prahran Netball representative described the site as an “ideal location.” Out of respect to Prahran Netball Representative her identity will remain private. Needless to say a serious breach of caretaker convention by an unelected Stonnington Council officer and possibly a. union member appears to have taken place.
 
As a result of the position that I and almost every other East Ward candidate has taken opposing the stadium at Percy Treyvaud, an email has been sent to all members of the Prahran Netball Association encouraging them to support a Labor candidate and direct their preferences to a Greens candidate. This email has been adapted and forwarded on by other sports clubs including the Malvern Tigers.

The Greens candidate is publicly on the record as opposing the Percy Treyvaud Stadium, but she we still benefit from Prahran Netball Association recommendation of support.  And it’s not just her. In fact the Prahran Netball Association is telling it’s members to preference the Greens in every ward across Stonnington! 

Malvern, Easr Malvern and Glen Iris there is a better way. If you support girls sport in East Ward and Netball in East Ward you do not need to sell your vote cheaply to Labor and the Greens. 

Vote for a parent who loves his daughter, loves girls sport and loves netball.

Vote for a Liberal, who takes his kids to sport, who plays sport, coaches kids sport and loves sport.

I am a candidate who is committed to delivering us indoor netball courts – at the right venue, not the wrong venue.

And I am not going to be a yes minister type councillor, being dictated to by unelected council bureaucrats about what can and can’t be done.

"I’ve lived in St Clair for over 40 years. Here, air circulation is restricted by Prospect Hill to the east and the Blue Mountains to the west. Heat gets trapped here and the air temperature rises very quickly. My local church - the Holy Spirit Parish Church – was built in the 1980s when insulation and cooling were not high on the agenda. 

During a Christmas Mass, my youngest child, Patrice, was asked to play Baby Jesus. She was only 12 days old so my wife, Margaret, played a guardian angel standing nearby in case our baby needed her mother. She was wearing a white gown and was so hot she almost fainted. I remember she was very red in the face and very thirsty.  

Over the years the heat during the summer months has become an area of great concern. Last year’s high temperatures became very dangerous. In December, it reached 48.9 degrees right here in Penrith.  

In response to high summer temperatures, our parish fundraised to purchase solar panels. It’s been such a relief. We can afford to run air conditioning and keep the church cool during summer. The electricity bills are much lower too."
- Peter Moriarty, Holy Spirit Parishioner

A record 38,000+ tests have been conducted in the past 24 hours and I am so proud of the way our community has risen to the challenge that has been thrown our way.

Thankfully the vast majority of new cases detected have been traced back to the initial Avalon RSL and Avalon Bowlo cluster, and I know I speak for all of us when I say that I marvel at the NSW Government and NSW Health’s capability set that has seen so many tested and tracked in record time.

Although we have seen a decrease in new daily cases today compared to yesterday, it is important that we all remain vigilant. #forthebeaches

Last night we were due to leave Stage 4.  Today we are still locked down.  Of course dates should not be used to measure lifting of restrictions, but neither should gross number of new cases and certainly not with a target of a two week daily average of 5.

Since leaving Stage 3, NSW has had a peak two week average of 13 new cases per day, which they have now managed back to 6.  Daniel Andrews has set the target of 5 before we can go into Stage 3, let alone leave it.  

Total elimination of the virus before a vaccine is unlikely, but elimination of jobs, businesses and people's life savings is well on track.  Of course, we need to aim for case minimisation so as not to overwhelm the health system or cause needless sickness or loss of life.  But 5 cases per day is an unnecessary target that is an over-reaction to their previous hotel quarantine debacle.

We need to keep in mind the infection rate (now well below 1) and differentiate from where cases are arising, like health care and aged care and address those problem areas with specific solutions.  And we should let other businesses open up now with appropriate safety protocols, even if they don't have militant unions bullying the Premier, like the building industry.   

Remember, emerging from lockdown did not cause Victoria's second wave.  Ongoing negligence in hotel quarantine, failing to recognise meat processing plants as high risk work environments (despite overseas evidence) and lack of control in the highly vulnerable aged care system did.  These factors quickly overwhelmed a scaled back and insufficient contact tracing capability and we are all left with the consequences.  

With adequate contact tracing, compulsory masks and appropriate rules on venue capacity and social distancing, there is no reason not to let us move toward a new covid normal.

As a child I remember stories about my great Aunt Betty (Betsy) - but they were through the eyes of a child - that she was a loving and generous person who was a great cook and made a mean cake. I didn’t know until this week that she was a pioneer in women’s representation in Council in New Zealand. (Thanks Aunty Debbie for pointing this out!)

Betty Eyre was elected to the Nelson City Council (NZ) as its first woman Councillor in 1956 serving 17 years in council including being deputy mayor for 9 years. In 1976 she was made an MBE for services to the community and local government.  

“It’s a testament to Betsy’s true community spirit that she continued to serve the Nelson community as a Councillor for so many years, and that she was honoured by the community with the naming of Betsy Eyre Park.

“It wasn’t until last year, some 63 years after Betsy was first elected, that a full gender balance around the Council table was reached. That’s a long time. But who knows how long it could have been without Betsy taking that first step.”

I hope I can do her proud

🛃 Ngân sách Liên Bang 2020 và chính sách nhập cư của Úc.

Ngày 6 tháng 10 năm 2020, chính phủ Úc công bố Ngân Sách Liên Bang 2020 với chính sách phục hồi và xây dựng lại nền kinh tế Úc cho tương lai. 

Trước tiên tôi xin chia sẻ về các ảnh hưởng của ngân sách năm nay đối với chính sách nhập cư của Úc như sau:  

✍️ Mặc dù chính phủ giữ số lượng visa nhập cư (Migration Planning Level) ở mức 160,000 chỗ, nhưng sự phân bổ các dạng visa nhập cư có rất nhiều thay đổi. 

✍️Lượng phân bổ cho visa tay nghề tự do (Independent), Bang bảo lãnh (State Nomination) và vùng miền (Regional) đều mất gần 50% chỗ so với tài khóa trước. 

✍️Visa tay nghề được doanh nghiệp bảo lãnh (Employer sponsored) giảm hơn 7,200 chỗ. 

✍️ Lượng phân bổ cho visa Nhân Tài (Global Talent) và visa kinh doanh đầu tư (Business Innovation & Investment) tăng hơn gấp 3 lần.

✍️Lượng phân bổ cho visa vợ chồng (Partner Visa) tăng gần gấp đôi từ 37,118 chỗ cho tài khóa trước lên 72,300 chỗ cho tài khóa năm nay. 

Theo thông tin công bố trong bản ngân sách và những thông báo của chính phủ Úc, tôi xin đưa ra nhận xét riêng của mình như sau:

🌟 Ngân sách năm nay là tin vui cho những đương đơn visa vợ chồng vì thời gian xét và cấp visa vợ chồng, đặc biệt những hồ sơ nộp tại Úc hoặc những đơn visa có người bảo lãnh sống tại vùng miền Úc có thể sẽ nhanh hơn. 

🌟 Theo tôi lượng tăng phân bổ cho visa vợ chồng này sẽ không lâu dài vì chính sách này giúp chính phủ lấp đầy lượng di dân đề ra trong lúc biên giới đóng cửa. Nhưng theo tôi nghĩ chính phủ sẽ quay trở lại chính sách ưu tiên cho di dân tay nghề để phục hồi nền kinh tế khi biên giới mở cửa trở lại.

🌟 Những đương đơn xin visa vợ chồng thường trú có thể sẽ gặp khó khăn nếu chính phủ áp dụng các đòi hỏi tiếng Anh hoặc học tiếng Anh trước khi cấp visa vợ chồng thường trú.

🌟 Visa tay nghề sẽ thay đổi theo hướng tập trung nguồn lực và tiềm lực cho việc phục hồi và phát triển kinh tế. Nguồn lực được tập trung cho các ngành trọng yếu và các ngành hỗ trợ cho đà hồi phục kinh tế trong tương lai. 

🌟 Vì vậy visa nhân tài và visa kinh doanh đầu tư có sự phân bổ tăng cao. Visa kinh doanh và đầu tư cũng sẽ được thay đổi vào khoảng tháng 7 năm 2021. Đây có thể là chính sách dài hạn vì chính phủ Úc đang cạnh tranh với các quốc gia khác trong việc thu hút nhân tài và các nhà đầu tư.

🌟 Visa tay nghề tự do, visa tay nghề Bang bảo lãnh hoặc visa tay nghề vùng miền sẽ mang tính chất cạnh tranh rất cao vì số lượng visa giới hạn. 

🌟 Visa tay nghề doanh nghiệp bảo lãnh có thể tăng trở lại nếu chính phủ mở cửa biên giới và nền kinh tế Úc phát triển trở lại.

No Kisses... No Buts

Like me you may have had the experience of trying to get an issue resolved with a Council Officer only to end up feeling that the person is 'all care but no responsibility'. The sense that they are saying 'yes that's terrible', 'yes I hear you' but that ultimately they are not going to take any action. I call that 'the kiss of yes'. It is alternately infuriating and demoralizing and I expect more from the Council staff who are paid to service our needs and respond to our concerns.

Then there have been occasions where I have run into the Officer who adopts a 'yes but it is not my area' or 'yes but its not in the budget'. The 'yes but' brush off is less infuriating/ demoralizing than the 'kiss of yes' but it is nonetheless disheartening.

Now of course while our rates pay for Council staff salaries they don't report to us; they report to their respective Team Leaders, Managers, Executive Managers and/or Directors. And these Executive Managers and Directors report to the CEO.

Councillors on the other hand do work for us; we elect them and they are accountable to their electorate. If elected I will not give you the 'kiss of yes'. I will not fob you off with 'yes but'. I am committing to being a 'Yes... and' Councillor. More than that I will use my role on Council to demand of the CEO that a culture of 'yes... and' starts to pervade the organization.

I understand organizations. I have been consulting in the area of organizational development, leadership and culture for over thirty years and I know that high performance starts with accountability. 

I will be accountable to you the electorate and I will drive hard to make the City of Yarra a responsive and accountable organization. Dare I say a 'Yes... and' organization.

Yes Council has done much that is to be commended and they could and should be doing more.

Yes I call the Melba Ward home and I will fight to protect, preserve and address the concerns of Cremorne, Burnley and Richmond First. What I lack in political experience I more than make up in organizational expertise and I will use that to address the culture of our Council because I don't know about y0u but I'm sick of 'kisses and buts!

ad_creative_body:
Non-compulsory voting
I can see no reason why, in a free society and democratic society, anyone should be compelled to vote and I certainly can’t see any good reason for punishing someone who chooses not to do so. If an individual cares so little about the political process or outcome, or has so little desire to support the candidates on offer, that they do not wish to participate then they should have the right to decline to participate if they so wish.

Right to Vote 1 ONLY
In time for the 2017 election the Queensland Labor party changed legislation so voters MUST number all boxes thereby allocating preferences for each nomination on the ballot paper. One can only imagine this was done to favour the major parties at the polls. As per my comments above, under “non-compulsory voting” I can see no reason why, in a free and democratic society, anyone who feels a political candidate or party is just plain unworthy of their vote should be compelled to vote for that person or party; regardless of the reason for their objection.

3 Party Preferred
As mentioned in my point above, under “Right to Vote 1 ONLY”, Queensland Labor changed legislation in time for the 2017 election to force voters to vote for each candidate in order from most to least preferred. It is my belief that this was done to rig things in the favour of the major parties (Labor, Liberal, and National) as eventually all votes flow to just 2 parties. As minor candidates lose their votes are then distributed to the majors, usually until only the majors are left standing. To reduce this election Stacking I feel a 3 party preferred system is more beneficial in reaching a result closer to the will of the people. By using a 3 party system a major party must rely less on the flow of preferences and more on gaining primary support from the electorate.
Our current political system does little to incentivise the major parties to aim to be anything better than the second worst option on offer.

Political Corruption
All politician expenses, all of them, from stationary to travel to meals etc to be publicly available on a real time system so the public and media can scrutinise them. If found to have taken advantage of public funds, or to have used public funds for personal use, the politician will be automatically removed from office. Some small allowances to be made here for politicians who genuinely made an error and for amounts less than $500.

Political Salaries
I propose that Politician salaries be linked to public service awards wages. Politicians salaries (pay raises) are to be linked to the lowest increase in award wages of any of its agencies. So if for instance the lowest state government body pay rise was for the Department of Transport and Main Roads and they are given a 2% increase, however every other state government body is given a 3% pay rise, our state government politicians will be awarded a 2% pay rise.

Political Superannuation Schemes
I propose that Politicians access to their superannuation is to be restricted in the same way as any other Australian, i.e. the funds are unavailable until the age of retirement. Further politicians superannuation is to be moved from a defined benefits scheme and replaced by an accumulation scheme, like the majority of Australians.

Political Donations
In recent times the issue of political donations is being raised on an increasingly frequent basis. People have mentioned how donations from industries like the tobacco industry have been banned because the money corrupts decision making and therefore corrupts government and government policy. In recent times a number of people or parties have suggested political donations from the firearms industry should also be banned, for the same reason, i.e. the money corrupts decision making, therefore corrupting government policy.

If donations from one group have a corrupting influence on government and the decisions it makes then it stands to reason that donations from ANY source corrupt government and the decisions is makes. Accordingly I propose a COMPLETE and ALL INCLUSIVE ban on ALL political donations from any source that is not a private individual. I also propose that all private donations be capped to no more than $200, inclusive of any party membership fees, that private political donations should only be allowed from people actually eligible to vote, and that ALL political fundraisers (such as fundraising dinners, you know the ones, when a party official shows up and charges attendees a substantial sum to dine in his or her presence) be banned.

To assist with the funding gap created by this policy I also propose that in place of donations EVERY candidate should be provided with a $5,000 campaign fund to be paid for by the state.

Limited Election Funding
As an Independent candidate for this election I have a cap on the amount of money I can spend which is UP TO $87,000. I don’t know whether this cap is the same or higher for registered parties but let’s face it $87,000 is a lot of money, especially for a party in a system with over 90 electorates. At 90 x $87,000 = $7,830,000 how is it possible for an independent to compete. I propose this cap should be lowered to $50,000, which even then still seems too high but is a move in the right direction.
While on the topic of state funding for elections, are you aware that for every Primary vote a major party receives they are paid $3.14. This money is however NOT guaranteed for minor parties or Independent candidates because each candidate needs to receive 6% of the primary vote to be eligible. This creates an uneven playing field and needs to be rectified. I propose that either these funds should cease to be offered or that all candidates receive this funding regardless of share of the primary vote.

PORTER ADMITTED LAW BIASED IN HIS FAVOUR

Australia’s defamation laws are broken. How do we know?
The Attorney General told us so.

In 2019, at the national press club in 2019, AG Christian Porter commented, “I think it is fair to say that current defamation laws no longer strike the perfect balance between public interest journalism and protecting individuals from reputational harm”.

He was launching the case for defamation law reform that would tilt the balance more in favour of protecting public interest journalism, and make it more difficult for the person claiming reputational damage. 

Fast forward to 2021 and Porter’s lawyers announced on Monday (the same day hundreds of thousand women marched for justice around Australia) that he is suing the ABC and journalist Louise Milligan for defamation under those same laws he has previously admitted are slanted in his (the plaintiff’s) favour.

“The trial by media should now end with the commencement of these proceedings,” Porter’s lawyers statement read.

“The claims made by the ABC and Ms Milligan will be determined in Court in a procedurally fair process.”

In announcing the defamation action , there was no mention of Porter’s previous criticism of the unbalanced defamation laws or how he reconciles that past criticism with his embrace of what he now calls a ‘procedurally fair process’ to end his so-called ‘trial by media’.

There is clearly a strong public interest in the public knowing that the nation’s first law officer (the Attorney general) has been accused of a serious crime.  Legal experts say however that under the current laws, a ‘public interest’ defence is unlikely to fly.

Furthermore, Porter has chosen to litigate in the Federal Court, fully aware that it is the jurisdiction known to most heavily favour the plaintiff (Porter).

A review of defamation law reform by the Parliamentary Library states “Arguably [there is] and incentive for some parties to litigate defamation actions in the Federal Court to avoid the involvement of a jury in proceedings.”

Porter wants you to believe that his defamation case will serve as a de facto ‘trial’ which would allow the opportunity for the ABC to prove the case against him “to the lower civil standard”.  The reality is, as Porter previously acknowledged, this ‘trial’ will be heavily weighted in his own favour. 

The other conveniently ignored elephant in the room is the problem of conflict of interest. How can Porter remain Attorney General with oversight of the Federal Court and judicial appointments, while he has a case heard in that same court? How can the judge overseeing the case act without perceptions of bias or self-interest? How can Christian Porter as Attorney General advocate for defamation law reform while at the same time using those laws he has criticised to his advantage.

By using defamation law as the vehicle to try and clear his name, 
Porter is amplifying the “chilling effect” that defamation law can have on the ability for journalists to hold powerful figures to account. 

When it comes to women’s rights to live safely and free of harassment, silence is said to equal violence. Using defamation law to scare off journalists from reporting such allegations perpetuates that silence. 

Porter can ensure he avoids all these problems and still take action to clear his name by asking his Prime Minister to set up an independent inquiry with a genuinely ‘procedurally fair’ process, while he stands aside.

An independent inquiry into whether Christian Porter is a fit and proper person to remain in his role is now needed more than ever. 

A retired judge or other suitably qualified person whom Porter has no oversight of, can be appointed to lead the inquiry.

Our petition to demand Scott Morrison set up such an inquiry now has over 10,000 signatures and growing: please sign and share here: change.org/christianporter

Thank you to everyone who has sent us your well-wishes over the past three weeks. I haven’t been able to respond to them all personally, but I can assure you I’ve read every single one!

Purpose Built Hospitals

I  have spoken extensively about the unacceptable issue of ambulance ramping and how this impacts on all Western Australians.
While both major political parties have acknowledged the situation, neither have come forward with a policy, proposal or solution that would alleviate the current situation.
I have previously stated on a number of occasions that the problem with a number of government services is that they are in need of an urgent operational review. Just allocating additional funds to a system that no longer provides the outcomes that are required by the community is irresponsible and a clear lack of leadership.

One of the major issues contributing to ambulance ramping is a significant increase in people presenting at hospital emergency rooms with mental health issues. Remember when these facilities were built the level of people presenting with mental health issues was minimal. It is time that we have purpose designed specific mental health emergency facilities. Firstly this will increase the quality of treatment for the patient with mental health issues but also alleviate the pressure placed on the emergency facility which could now focus on individuals with physical health conditions. These purpose built mental health facilities could be built adjacent to existing emergency facilities or as a standalone service within the community. These facilities would be staffed with dedicated mental health professionals. People may not be aware but currently the majority of emergency room staff are not adequately trained in the treatment of mental health and have chosen to focus primarily on general medicine. This results in the patient not receiving the highest level of care possible and emergency room staff not being utilised in providing services they are fully trained for.

We constantly hear how much more needs to be done regarding mental health treatment within Western Australia. The above proposal would be a significant first step in rectifying the shortcomings of the existing system.

If you are a medical professional who can enlighten us further on this topic please do not hesitate in sharing your experiences and views.

Dale.

The land on which Towerhill sits was sold by council to private owners back in 1995 for an undisclosed amount. Council is proposing to change the status of the roads through the centre meaning that they can be developed upon. Council will receive no money for this status change even though council has been providing upkeep on these roads from at least 2015. 

Currently residents can use the roads in Towerhill shopping centre to connect between Bondi Avenue through to Frankston-Flinders and Golf Links Rd. The planned road status changes will give developers full control of these roads and allow for them to decide how local residents can access the shopping complex. 

Development is an important part of making Frankston a better place to live. But only if the benefits to the community outweigh the costs. Bayside Shopping Centre is a classic example of poor decision making by council where community assets were sold off and then Frankston residents were stung by having to pay to park there. 

Cr Steven and Liam Hughes call on Frankston council and the property developers to provide full details of any proposed changes to accessibility at the Towerhill shopping centre. Residents have a right to know the details of any decision that will impact their daily lives. Only then will we be satisfied that the interests of Frankston residents are being put first.

BREAKING! SOUTH AUSTRALIA RECOGNISES THE REPUBLIC OF ARTSAKH, CONDEMNS AZERBAIJAN AND TURKEY

South Australia became the second state in Australia to recognise the rights to self-determination of the Republic of Artsakh, condemning Azerbaijan and Turkey for their invasion of the country's indigenous Armenians in a motion passed with a vote in the House of Assembly, reported the Armenian National Committee of Australia (ANC-AU).

The motion follows one passed by the New South Wales Parliament's Legislative Assembly in October 2020, and similarly "calls on the Federal Government to also recognise the Republic of Artsakh as the only permanent solution to the conflict to avoid further attempts of such military aggression".

Member for West Torrens, the Hon. Tom Koutsantonis MP moved the historic motion, which also called out "the actions of President Erdogan of Turkey and President Aliyev of Azerbaijan in their pursuit of a policy of Pan-Turkish nationalism, which has previously led to genocide and which now threatens the Armenian population of Artsakh with ethnic cleansing".

The House of Assembly considered a proposal to "adjourn the debate", however this was defeated by the casting vote of the Speaker. The debate resumed and resulted in a vote – without dissent – in favour of the motion.

ANC-AU Executive Director Haig Kayserian thanked the Armenian Cultural Association of South Australia (ACASA) for their grassroots advocacy.

"We were proud to support members of Adelaide's dedicated Armenian community for their tireless efforts on the ground, which have ensured South Australia's parliament has joined a growing number of legislatures around the world supporting the legitimate rights to self-determination of the Republic of Artsakh," said Kayserian.

"Mr Emil Davityan and the President of the Armenian Cultural Association of South Australia are a credit to the greater Armenian-Australian community and were a pleasure to work with to achieving this wonderful outcome for our heroic brothers and sisters of the Armenian Republic of Artsakh," he added.

Emil Davityan added: "We thank Mr Tom Koustantonis and Ms Jayne Stinson for championing this motion and extend our gratitude to all parliamentarians who supported its passage in the name of human rights."

"South Australia's Armenian community wanted to play its part in supporting the people of Artsakh, bringing attention to the critical humanitarian issues in the region and contributing to an enduring and peaceful settlement to the conflict. The community thanks all who supported it in its endeavours."
