Hi all,

So I can’t help myself I just keep seeing things that don’t quite look right within Council, so I write about them. I have to be grateful because the Courier mostly provides me with space. I do have to thank them but I have to complain about the propensity they have to edit out the best bits, the most meaningful bits.

On Monday they published my latest rant along with a big picture of my ugly mug. Thanks Mr Editor but why did you have to cut out the most significant piece of the offering – very frustrating.

So here is the uncut version. GT
 

The Editor,

The Courier,

Sir,

I write once again to raise the matter of now three recent Council inquiries and reports. I note they are about to be joined by a fourth with the decision from Janet Dore to refer all the three reports to Council’s Audit and Risk Committee. For mine it is starting to get to the point of “ho hum” which is a shame, actually by now the entire issue has become rather meaningless – most certainly nothing has been resolved.

Initially these reports were lauded by media as spectacular expose’s of all that was wrong within Council. Real fact was there was nothing new things had been wrong for a long time. I suspect that none of the several Council watchers who had regularly haunted the Town Hall prior to the 2016 Council election would have found anything new or surprising in what was revealed, the difficulty then, as now, has always been getting Council to understand and accept there are issues.
 

My belief is that few of the members of the 2016 elected Council had any idea that they were effectively sitting on a time bomb the fuse to which had been set a long time before. As a “watcher” of long standing I was definitely aware there were issues, and upon election to Council went to great pains get on the Contracts Sub Committee on the basis of a misguided belief that as a Councilor I would be able to play a role in sorting things out. How wrong was I?
 

Notwithstanding all the “Who Ha”, Sitting here today it would be reasonable to prognosticate that all the issues which caused the recent problems and which were properly identified during “the inquisitions”, generally still exist today, and continue to affect the good operation of our Council much as before, notwithstanding all of the furor, upheavals and departures.

Without doubt all of the issues of note, then and now, have their genesis in one word - “Procurement”. Council procurement of items, big and small when mixed with what is effectively the “contempt for the Community dollar” shown by Officers by way of not always seeking outcomes which are in the best commercial interest of the Community – this is where the whole issue starts and finishes - in all things the protection of the Community dollar must be sacrosanct and the proper accounting for the spending of that dollar is critical.  

The three reports which have been tabled – Ombudsman – Pitcher Partners – Halliday - all demonstrate discoveries of various system failures, but at the same time all three missed understanding the critical issue of proof, and none really provided guidance as to a remedy. What the reports did do, and very effectively, was to trash reputations, with no right of reply. From any perspective they were at best disgracefully expensive “Hit and Run” exercises which held no regard for truth or Natural Justice. Thick on inuendo, thin on proof.

Notwithstanding any beliefs the Community might hold about the role and the authority of a Councilor to have knowledge of really what was, or is, going on within the organization - Councilors really have none. Worse yet via the new local Government Act still have none, in fact even less than before. Your Councilors – your Community appointed watchdogs - are actively denied access to critical information under the umbrella of the provisions within a number of Acts of Parliament. Accordingly it can be argued there was not one item which was covered in any of the reports that any Councilor could have done anything about – Flowers, Fruit and Chandeliers (three of them) included. The machine which is “Council”, whether the Acting C.E.O. is prepared to accept or not, was always in charge.

Within the organization the actual blame and fault really lies totally through the inability of the procurement systems of Council to control, regulate, and monitor, what goes on within the organization and there is little doubt the faults identified in the reports remain active today, these numerous reports notwithstanding. The tragedy of all of it all is that the reports thus far tabled have played “the Man” (Woman), not “the Ball” and have clearly done so with some malice, yet have failed to identify and offer corrections for the issues – not one of the reports even comes close to correctly identifying the root causes of the myriad of issues revealed. I am prepared to bet the fourth report, which Janet Dore has just announced in a last gasp attempt to justify and vindicate her term in the chair, won’t produce any better result.

In a nutshell my the view is, that all of the issues of the Council, revealed or not revealed by reports done, or proposed to be done, all dance around two root issues – First:- The RESPECT for the Community shown by “The Council” via the systems which make up the organization. At all times and in all things full respect MUST be afforded the residents while protecting their best interests. Respect is an unusual word, with many connotations, but the most fundamental way in which respect manifests itself in this context is through the proper spending of Community money, not just on things but also on wages (people, workers). The expenditure of money on wages MUST be predicated upon those in the employ of Council at all levels honoring the terms of their engagement, performing just those tasks they are given, and not coveting the jobs of others. Clearly it includes a responsibility for those in charge to look after those beneath them in the tree, including provision of opportunities for progress and personal enhancement, but only on merit and importantly only as opportunities arise, and Second:- The RESPECT the organization shows, MUST SHOW, to the Councilors of the day in their role as the “Leaders of the Community by virtue of the fact they are the elected “watch dogs” representing the Community”.

Senior Officers of Council, and even some of the lower lights, have wide ranging powers via the delegations they are given, in trust, by the Councilors including the spending of money. They must remember those delegations are a privilege, not a right. Those delegations must be treated with care and professionalism and must never be used on the whim of an Officer, or even a group of them, without due regard for the efficacy of what they are setting out to do. Interestingly just in the last few days a large amount of money (maybe as much as $500,000 or so) began to be expended, I believe completely unbeknown to any Councilor. Cash which it could, should, be argued was not spent wisely. Now the system says that’s OK, BUT, I bet it was never run past the sitting Council, let alone the Ward Councilors – the project most certainly must have been in the planning stage during my time in Council but I knew nothing of it (and would have questioned it heavily if I had known) - so Janet Dore and all, Ombudsman’s Report notwithstanding, Pitcher Partners Report for what it was worth, and now a Fourth report which has been called for, and heaps of sackings and resignations and we still, in my view, have goings on about which the Councilors are sublimely ignorant, in fact are deliberately shielded from knowledge. No Councilor can fight a fight, or properly represent their constituents with both hands tied behind their back.

The fundamental question which must be answered is “Just who is in charge of the City of Ballarat and for what purpose” ?

To the new Chief Executive Officer, your task awaits! – I am afraid the work is not complete. Good Luck.

Support Local Businesses Series

Meet Mr Vince Vari
 
Mr Vari, better know as ‘Vince’, started Varis Fruit & Vegetable shop in Barkly St, West Footscray in 1965.
It is one of the oldest standing businesses in West Footscray.
 
Vince was born in Calabria, Italy, which is at the toe of the boot, the extreme south of Italy.
 
He migrated to Australia at the age of 21 and settled down in the western suburbs. He worked at the Footscray Market in a friend’s business for about 6 years. before
opening one of the first fruit and vegetable stores in West Footscray at the age of 27.
 
At the outset he had competition, as three other fruit & vegetable stores opened up in competition.
 
Four years into his business Vince purchased his building for $23,000, and set about arranging fresh produce for the locals.
 
His business flourished as his daily routine of getting up at 3am to get vegetables from the market kept him enthused.
 
He loved the locals (and still does) so much that it earned him the ‘goss-king’ title, as he was the man with the know in the area. He was the local news channel.
 
Vince recalls the days when all the other shop owners knew each other, and there were 4 major banks in the Barkly shopping strip. The friendly managers and staff would often stop by and have a chat with him, and everyone knew each others’ names.
 
He use to trade 6 days a week and remembers when people shopped with paper bags and boxes only, and when entire families would come out to shop.
 
The highlight of Vince’s day used to be chatting with the locals.
“They were friendly locals and I’ve missed seeing them and talking to them since lockdown started. I’m really looking forward to seeing all the locals again and chatting with them about their life in lockdown”.
 
Vince is an avid Western Bulldogs fan.
He use to go to every Bulldogs game until the Whitten Oval was decommissioned. After that he used to hand out his tickets to customers to go and watch the games.
 
He was a big sponsor of the club, assisting them every week with fruit and other needs when the club wasn’t doing too well.
Sadly Vince knew the Bulldogs wouldn’t  win the premiership this year!
 
Vince’s son, Rino Vari, took over the store in 2002, just as a trial year to help Vince. 18 years on Reno has successfully manoeuvered the business to become the only full time Organic store in West Footscray, and offers online sales and home deliveries.
 
Due to Covid restrictions it’s been extremely difficult for their small business to keep replenishing the ‘display stock’ on a daily basis and hence the store is currently only trading online for home deliveries. They hope to reopen after lock down ends.
 
55 years on Varis fruit & Vegetables has turned into Varis Organics, but the aura, the friendliness, the fresh produce and other amazing products continue to thrive.
 
For online ordering please head to:
www.varisorganics.com.au

Support local businesses during these unprecedented times and they will continue supporting us when community needs arise.

At the December council meeting I requested that the Mayor ✍️ to Premier Steven Marshall and relevant State Ministers expressing the City of Salisbury, deep concern and requesting urgent action by the State Government to investigate and remedy the issues relating to the rapidly declining health of the mangroves.

The Department for Energy and Mining has issued the following update today:

Update on St Kilda mangroves - Tuesday 12 January 2021

Government shares community concerns regarding the environment surrounding the salt fields, and is focused on stabilising the site in both the short and long term.

Stablising the Dry Creek salt fields is a government priority, with several regulatory actions currently underway.

The regulator has issued three directions:
1. To stop pumping water into ponds
2. To address seepage at Para River
3. Remove water from the 7 km ponds south of St Kilda

The site operator is working to rectify the issues and is being responsive to directions from Government.

Government regulators are actively monitoring the site, including vegetation mapping and hydrological analysis.

Formal investigation into the cause of the mangrove dieback and any compliance actions continues.

•Establish a specific taskforce including local traders associations, councillors and council executives to identify the URGENT needs of local business.

Do you think I should re-stand for council?

This October will mark eight years since I was first elected as a Councillor, at the youthful age of just 24 years old. 

Those of you who are good at arithmetic will have deduced that I'm now 32 (and perhaps not so young anymore) 🙈. 

📱 Lately, I’ve received a lot of messages asking why I haven't announced my candidacy for the Ballarat Council election yet- the truth is, I haven't decided. 

In fact- I'd really love to know your thoughts.

I've spent a lot of time over the past few months reflecting on my time on council, including the things I'm proud of, as well as what I've learnt. 

I'd love to share some of them with you.

✅ One of the things I'm most proud of is voting against every rate rise that's been put before me. 

I was beyond ecstatic this year when my advocacy finally paid off and we passed a 0% rate rise- it’s just a pity that it took a global pandemic to achieve it. 

✈️ I’m also pleased to share that I’ve never used rate payers money to fly overseas on a council junket either. 

🌱 When I look back on my time as Councillor- I'm especially proud of the delivery of our Green Waste Service - a project I spearheaded.

🛋 Next on the list is a bi-annual hard-rubbish collection!!

My highlights from the past couple of years include:

👉 Securing major events such as Spilt Milk, White Night and the Cycling Australia Road Nationals

👉 Delivering the Ballarat Link Road

👉 Commencing work to completely revitalise and redevelop the Bridge Mall

👉 Committing to council achieving carbon neutrality and to be powered 100% by renewables by 2025

👉 Delivery of the Lucas Community Hub

👉 Securing funding $3.7 million in funding for Alfredton Recreation Reserve

👉Delivering Ballarat's first Inclusive Playspace at Victoria Park

❤️ The most rewarding part of my job has without doubt been helping people.

Whether its help getting a road sealed, with navigating council services, funding requests for sporting clubs or community groups or perhaps another fenced dog park. 

Helping people has been the aspect I've enjoyed the most- because it's given me the opportunity to connect with so many fantastic people... many of whom have gone on to become my friends. 

🤔 So what do you think - should I put my hand up to serve another four years- meaning (if re-elected) I'll be (gasp) 36 by the time my term is completed! 

I'd love to hear your thoughts...

My father used to be a banker back in Lebanon but had to escape here during the civil war. When he migrated to Australia, he worked in local factories before finally marrying my mum, who was a teacher in Syria. My mum had no proper English-speaking background when she moved down to Australia. They decided to open their own pizza shop business in East Brighton that we owned for over 20 years. She soon had my brother and I a year later, and slowly learned how to speak English watching Play School and Thomas the Tank Engine alongside us. 

She raised us with no family around her, while working long hours in our Pizza shop. She supported my father while running a household and raising my brothers and I, picking up whatever English she could. From 13 years old, my brothers and I would come home from school and help in the shop.

For years, my parents worked extremely hard, working 7 days a week, and sacrificed a lot to make sure my brothers and I had the best education we could afford. They valued our education and setting up our future before their own. I attended St James College in East Bentleigh and then St Bedes College in Mentone. They supported us through university, where my brother was one of the first in our family to graduate from University with a double degree in Mechatronics Engineering and Commerce from Monash. I graduated shortly after with a Bachelor of Software Engineering.

My parents taught me the value of not taking things for granted and to take every opportunity that came our way to better ourselves. They also showed me the meaning of hard work, selflessness and caring for others. In particular, looking out for those who did not have the luxury of support networks like: a community or religious group; or close friends or; family.

While I was at Monash University, these values led me to become involved with my Student Union. I was privileged to be elected as the People of Colour Officer for the Monash Student Association and then again, the year after as the Executive General Representative also serving as Secretary. Here I worked to better student life on campus, promote opportunities for people of colour, and revitalise the vibrancy and campus community culture at Clayton.

Now, I say all this, obviously, because I want to introduce myself and let you all know more about where I come from, how my story is that of the typical multicultural Australian family struggle. But also, because I want you to know what my values are, what I stand for and why I am choosing to run.

I am blessed that I have a strong family to support me and even more blessed to have a close community to grow with. I’ve lived in Clarinda for nearly 20 years, the best days of my childhood were spent playing football out in the court with my neighbours, tennis at the Clarinda Tennis Club or down in the park at Drushi Crt Reserve in Clarinda. But as I have gotten older, I see more and more how our sense of community is slipping away from us. How our councillors, who were elected to make our community better, our homes safer and carry our rates further are more concerned with how they can do the bare minimum and in some instances nothing at all, to get re-elected.

Help me make Kingston a community focused council again.

COVID 5-DAY SHUTDOWN 
Beginning at 6pm tonight, the whole Perth metropolitan area, the Peel region and the South West region will be going into a full lockdown.

This lockdown will run until 6pm on Friday.

A five-day lockdown.

The following measures will be put in place from 6pm for people in Perth, Peel and the South West:

People in these regions are required to stay home, except for the following four reasons:

- Shopping for essentials like groceries, medicine and necessary supplies.

- Medical or health care needs including compassionate requirements and looking after the vulnerable.

- Exercise, within their neighbourhood, but only with one other person and only for one hour per day.

- Work, where you cannot work from home or remotely.

In addition to this Stay Home rule.

If you do leave home, for one of the four reasons you will be required to wear a mask at all times outside and if you need to work indoors, then wearing a mask in the workplace is also mandatory.

Mask wearing on public transport is also mandatory.

People in the Perth, Peel or South West region need to stay inside their region for the next five days, unless for an essential reason.

The State Government are strongly encouraging that everyone in this area, who is from another WA region, stay here and do not travel further outside of this area until the lockdown is over.

If you do need to travel outside the region you are in now, that can only occur if you need to return to your place of residence or exceptional circumstances.

The transport of essential goods into this region, is permitted, under our existing transport guidelines.

This lockdown means the following businesses, venues and locations in the relevant regions need to close for the next five days:

- Pubs, bars and clubs

- Gyms and indoor sporting venues

- Playgrounds, skate parks and outdoor recreational facilities

- Cinemas, entertainment venues, and casinos

- Large religious gatherings and places of worship

- Libraries and cultural institutions

Restaurants and cafes will close, and provide takeaway service only.

10 people can attend funerals, weddings are cancelled for the next five days.

No visitors are permitted to your home, unless caring for someone vulnerable or an emergency.

No visitors will be allowed in aged care homes, unless exceptional circumstances.

No visitors to hospitals and/or disability facilities, unless exceptional circumstances.

Elective surgery and procedures for categories 2 and 3 will be suspended from Tuesday, 2 February. Category 1 and urgent category 2 surgery will continue.

For a majority of schools in these regions, school was due to start tomorrow.

That has now been put on hold and schools will be closed until next week – following the lockdown measures.

It is, in effect, an extension of the school holidays.

All these measures will be reviewed regularly and the Chief Health Officer will continue to monitor the serious situation and provide more ongoing advice.

Western Australians have done so well for so long but this week it is absolutely crucial that we stay home, maintain physical distancing and personal hygiene and get tested if you have symptoms.

This is a very serious situation and each and every one of us has to do everything we personally can to help stop the spread in the community.

Ever wondered how the electorate of Cooper got its name? 

To mark Women’s History Month during March, I thought I’d share with you the fascinating story of Dr Lilian Violet Cooper, whom the Cooper electorate is named after.

Dr Cooper, who emigrated from England to Brisbane in 1891, was the first woman doctor registered in Queensland, and within months, the first woman doctor in Brisbane to have her own surgery.

On 9 June 1891 the first advertisement of consultation hours for Dr Lilian Cooper appeared in the Brisbane Courier.

At the time the profession was very dominated by men; but historical records show she was a strong, determined woman who forged her own path in life, and was a woman of many firsts.

She was one of the first women in Queensland to own a motorcar, which she taught herself to drive and maintain. 

In a very interesting story, in 1909 Dr Cooper and Dr Hardie, her fellow medical officer at the Lady Lamington Women’s Hospital, were fined £3/3/6 (a week’s wages at the time) for speeding down Queen Street, clocking over the 6 miles per hour limit.

During her career she had her own practice, and she worked at the Hospital for Sick Children and the Lady Lamington Hospital for Women in Brisbane, before joining the Mater Misericordiae Hospital in 1905.

During World War I, Cooper volunteered with the Scottish Women's Hospital Service after she was turned down by the Australian Army as female doctors were not wanted. She worked on the frontline in France and Serbia and was in charge of the ambulance division run by all female drivers.

After her return from the war, Lilian continued with her practice and her work at the hospitals, living at Kangaroo Point. She helped found the Royal Australasian College of Surgeons in 1928. 

Dr Cooper died at Brisbane in August 1947 and is buried next to her long-time companion Mary Josephine Bedford at Toowong Cemetery.

As you can see, Dr Cooper was an amazing woman - incredibly strong, selfless and a fierce advocate for women. We honour her and all the other amazing women like her who helped shape the many freedoms and rights we enjoy today.

This year, in the lead up to Reconciliation week, Rio Tinto detonated explosives and destroyed 46,000 year old caves at the Juunkan Gorge in the Pilbara region of Western Australia. The destruction of these important Aboriginal sites unleashed waves of shock, grief and anger across the country. A Joint Standing Committee has been appointed to investigate whether Australian heritage laws protect Indigenous cultural heritage and pressure is mounting on governments to ensure that heritage laws are fit for purpose.  

In NSW, 32 mining projects are in the pipeline. Government departments argue that these projects are vital to the state’s economic recovery. Three of these mining projects are located on Gomeroi country – in the North West plains region of NSW.

This seminar focuses on Gomeroi peoples’ ongoing campaign to stop the Shenhua Watermark mine in Gunnedah. In 2015, Aunty Dolly Talbott filed an application on behalf of Gomeroi people to protect and declare Significant Areas of country that are at risk of obliteration if Shenhua mine goes ahead. The Federal Minister for Environment acknowledged the ‘immeasurable cultural values’ of the Gomeroi sites but ultimately declined to protect them, finding that the mine’s potential economic and social benefits outweighed their heritage value. In 2020, Aunty Dolly took legal action against the Minister but the appeal failed in the Federal Court.  

In this seminar, Aunty Dolly Talbott, Nadja Zimmermann (Environmental Defenders Office), Tony McAvoy SC (Frederick Jordan Chambers), and Tim Buckley (Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis) discuss: how can short-term economic outcomes from mining outweigh the protection of culturally important sites? What cultural heritage reforms are needed to better protect ancient sites of immeasurable value? What are the alternatives to coal mining on Gomeroi country?

Hundreds of Australians have participated in the Armenian National Committee of Australia’s (ANC-AU) #EndYourSilence social media campaign, aimed at spreading awareness about Azerbaijan’s attacks on the Republic of Artsakh and to call out the Federal Government and national media for their "death-ening silence".

On 27th September 2020, Azerbaijan – backed by Turkey who deployed Islamist Jihadist terrorists and provided air support – launched a wide-scale offensive along the entire Artsakh border. The #EndYourSilence social media campaign saw members of the Armenian-Australian community standing in solidarity with Armenia and Artsakh by taking photos with their hands covering their mouths, protesting the oil-billions and diplomatic threats that gagged Australia from their commitment to speak out for human rights.

By sharing the campaign on social media platforms, along with the infographic of facts and instructions outlining the purpose of the campaign, it allowed for greater use of voices to reach as many people as possible.

Abram is a senior marketing professional with 14 years’ experience working across a variety of brands, verticals and within B2B and B2C environments. With a passion and focus on digital channels, her strategic thinking was a driving force behind the creation of the campaign.

Why does the party exist?
- - - - - -
The party was formed in response to a grass-roots movement, where people couldn’t see themselves represented by existing parties driven by out-dated ideologies. All members and candidates have a core belief that politics should be about progress, and that progress should be underpinned by common-sense values. We want to break the cycle that results in the major parties dominating our current political system.

 
How will we Canberra Progressives deliver?
- - - - - -
Any Canberra Progressives candidates elected will provide an ethical, evidence-based check on everything the government does or plans to do. We will provide the platform and framework for the community to have a real say in what is going on. We will listen to new ideas, plans and needs for the future of our city direct from the community.

 
Why should voters vote for the Canberra Progressives and their candidates?
- - - - - -
Canberra Progressives will provide a fresh new voice in the assembly which will focus on people-centred, community-driven progress. If elected our commitment to the electorate is to ensure every policy, decision and action from the government will be ethical, show evidence that it is the right thing to do and will be in the best interest of the community.

 
What makes Canberra Progressives different?
- - - - - -
Canberra Progressives comprise members from all walks of life united under our three core principles: Ethics. Evidence. Empowerment. We don’t have any vested interests from donors, lobby groups or supporters. We proudly have the most transparent and ethical party donations and funding rules in the ACT, if not the country. We are a party for all, not just a few. All members have the same voting rights, opportunities and responsibilities.

 
Does the Canberra Progressives have any real chance of winning a seat?

Our major parties have indeed created a political system that favours them over any new parties or independents. That’s partly why we have had 20 years of Labor in government.  The world continues to change, and so should our political system. We urge voters to vote Canberra Progressives first, and major parties further down the list. If this happens we will have a great chance of winning a seat and truly holding the government to account.

 
Would the Canberra Progressives support Liberal or Labor to form government?
- - - - - -
As a party created to empower the community and members, we would take this question to the party membership. We would trust our members to decide which major party best aligns with our party principles and values of Ethics, Evidence and Empowerment.

 
Isn’t Canberra one of the most progressive cities in Australia? So why do we need a new progressive party?

Yes, the ACT is progressive, and there have been some good initiatives, especially around climate change activities and programs. But the city is going backwards in many critical areas, including housing developments, health services, support for small business, and community connectivity.

I have been hearing a lot of talk and queries around the dog waste bags provided by the City and many are asking why don't we use bio-degradable bags at The City of Canning?... here's the answer:

Based on the City’s current two bin waste collection system (with NO Food Organics and Garden Organics collection for compostable waste) it is not feasible from a cost or environmental perspective to change our dog bags to compostable bags. This is due to the following:
 
1️⃣   When the compostable bags are released into the environment as litter, the bags do not break down as designed. The bags persist in the environment and degrade into smaller pieces, which can be over a period of 12 months or more, still presenting an environmental hazard to wildlife and natural areas.
2️⃣  When compostable bags are sent to landfill, they also do not break down as designed, and release methane into the atmosphere during the process of breaking down. When compostable bags are sent to an industrial composting facility, they are broken down as designed due to optimised temperatures and the presence of specific microorganisms, who then ‘feed’ on the bags and release CO2 – a much less harmful greenhouse gas than methane.
3️⃣   If/when the City does move to a FOGO system, then compostable bags will definitely be considered as a potential feasible option to replace the current yellow plastic bags.
 
Degradable bags simply break down into smaller pieces and become micro plastics. These bags offer the worst option in terms of cost and environmental outcomes, even when considering our current yellow plastic dog bags.

For more information, check out this article....

Brads 5 Point Plan #3: Traffic And Roads Management.

This is an issue I know a thing or two about. I have been licensed to drive heavy commercial vehicles for over 17 years now and I know that big trucks and some roads just do not work together. The Northern end of Browns Road in Noble Park North is one such example. 

In February 2018, VicRoads Movement And Safety Manager, Sasha Yarwood told the Dandenong Journal that modifying the intersection of Browns Road and Police Road in Noble Park North to accommodate trucks would require property acquisition and would result in more trucks using surrounding streets. To be fair, she is probably right. That is why there is only one genuine option. 

The industrial zone of Browns Road is located exclusively at the Southern end of Browns Road just off the Princes Highway. There are simply no reason why large trucks cannot use major nearby roads like Springvale Road or Eastlink to access Princes Highway and access Browns Road from an appropriate and safe intersection. Therefore, I will strongly advocate for a total ban on large trucks entering Browns Road from Police Road. Truck bans have worked successfully on Beach Road in Melbourne's Bayside suburbs, they have worked successfully in Yarraville, there is no reason why they cannot work in Noble Park North. 

In addition to truck movements, I have also received a lot of correspondence from residents regarding the need to traffic taming solutions for some residential streets to help prevent the prevalence of hoon drivers and speeding in residential streets. This is a commitment I will make if elected to investigate and advocate for solutions in known trouble areas so that our residential streets remain safe for all residents, especially families with kids and the elderly. 

For A Better Greater Dandenong - Vote 1 Brad Woodford.

Hi, I’m Jo Cicchini, your Liberal Candidate for Midland.

I was born at Swan Districts Hospital and raised locally in the Swan area. I am married to my husband Mark and we have three children.

Our family loves living, working and studying in the eastern suburbs.

I’m a proud small business owner and run my own hair salon. I meet people from all walks of life and get to listen and understand the issues that matter most to them and their families. I’m a member of the Swan and Mundaring Chamber of Commerce.

My husband Mark also runs his own small business as a Carpenter and has always worked in the construction industry.

Building my own small business from the ground up, I’m living the challenges and rewards that small and family-run businesses in Midland experience every day. We need to keep our local small businesses open and locals in work.

As part of the Liberal team, I’ll fight for more local police to make our streets and suburbs safer, tackle the McGowan Government’s unfair $850 per year increases to fees and charges and I’ll be a voice for better education opportunities for our youth.

We need to make sure our young people can access the education and jobs training they need locally, so they can continue to live, study and work in the eastern suburbs.

I am fighting against the proposed Robinson Road closure in Bellevue/Midland, for Labor's Metronet Railcar Facility. I want to support our local businesses in our Blue Collar Industrial Area, so that we can all work together and share this space.

I also understand and have lived in this area and know full well, the terrible impact on surrounding roads and quiet suburbs and the traffic congestion it will cause if Robinson Road is shut down.

I am determined to deliver solutions for our homelessness problem in Midland. The Liberal Party already have a plan for 500 fully supported interim accommodation beds across Perth.

I am a big supporter and want to advocate for our Stratton and surrounding communities for safe pedestrian access on Farrall Rd, including a safe railway crossing. I am 100% behind Stratton community groups and sporting groups and want to see activities around the Stratton oval, grow.

I want to work on that inadequate mobile phone reception in Caversham.

I want to advocate for the residents of Swan View and Greenmount, who live close to our tourist attractions.

I want to tackle Meth and all the problems that it brings and the underlying problems before that.

I want to support families.

I’m concerned about the declining state of the old Swan Districts Hospital. It has been left for far too long, making it a target for anti-social behaviour. We need to revitalise the area and return it to our community.

I am the eldest of 6 children. I learned to contribute, share, work hard and serve our community from a very young age.

I have a strong family connection with Midland, with my Great-grandfather, George Tate, settling in Midland in the 1920's. George played in the Midland Symphony Orchestra. Relatives worked at the Midland Westrail Workshops, the abattoirs, Hutton's Meats and the skin sheds. 

In 1977, my parents were the first to build in Clayton Estate Bellevue. I attended the same local school as my father, Koongamia Primary School and attended Swan Christian and Swan View High.

I was a gymnast at the Midland Police & Citizens Club, played netball at Harper Park in West Midland and worked for many years in retail at Midland Gate and Centrepoint.

I believe in Midland and its people. I am passionate about making our community a fantastic place to live, work and raise a family.
I believe in working with locals to deliver results and will fight for the issues that matter most to you and your family.

It’s time for a change! It's time for new energy! We need a passionate, local voice. I will work hard and will fight for Midland in State Parliament, if given an opportunity.

I am Born, Bred and have a genuine heart for Midland. 

Please get in contact with me to discuss local issues - I'm here to help and look forward to hearing from you.

The RePlant Byron community forest is a unique initiative that will help improve land quality, restore biodiversity, help stabilise the water table and provide a valuable community resource.
 
Zero Emissions Byron is a volunteer run community project, with six working groups who meet regularly. There are five groups which cover the different sectors of emissions (energy, buildings, waste, land use and transport), plus a communications working group.

I congratulate Zero Emissions on this wonderful project and their ongoing passion and commitment to environmental conservation, community engagement and reducing emissions. I’m incredibly proud to support local environmental groups such as Zero Emissions who focus on positive outcomes by improving the extent, connectivity and condition of native vegetation that in turn supports native species.

The federal funding has gone towards site preparation and purchase of approximately 2400 native trees including Figs, Lilly Pillies and Red Cedar. Volunteers and participants will be onsite for the RePlant Byron community forest planting which is scheduled for ‪Saturday 19th September‬ across a one-hectare site.
 
We’re so fortunate to have such active, committed and diverse community groups across our region and I look forward to working together to make our area an even better place to live.
 
The Richmond Communities Environment Programme supports small scale, community-led environment projects that address environmental priorities across the North Coast which give our community the resources, skills and knowledge to care for the environment.
 
I’ll always fight to get our fair share from Canberra. This funding is part of the more than $2 billion that I’ve delivered for local roads, schools, health and community resources.

EXPRESS BUSES TO FRANKSTON COMING SOON

I've been catching the buses on the Mornington Peninsula for much of my life. I know the Mornington Peninsula Public Transport Network all too well, and it consistently ranks as one of the main issues you all raise with me. 

Today, we have some exciting news.

Starting soon, Route 887 between Rosebud and Frankston will be realigned via the Mornington Peninsula Freeway, in a huge development for the Mornington Peninsula's public transport system.

Additionally, the frequency of Route 788 from Frankston to Portsea will be increased from a 40-50 minute frequency to a 30 minute frequency on weekdays, and upgraded to a 40 minute frequency on weekends – helping to tackle crowding and giving passengers more choice about when they travel.

Finally, people living in Dromana and Mount Martha will also see better access to buses with the extension of Route 781 to Dromana.

These changes will support locals who rely on buses to get to work, school or university, medical services and social events as well as connecting visitors to tourist attractions and onwards public transport at Frankston Station.

The Mornington Peninsula is a major holiday destination, and when tourists visit in the warmer months to enjoy the beaches, food and wine and markets, travel time increases and some services get extremely crowded.

This funding will support tourism in the region by increasing weekend services on Route 788 during the summer, as well as updating the timetable with more accurate journey times during this busier period to reflect the increased traffic on the roads that can slow down buses.
The changes are taking place as part of the Labor Government’s Bus Network Improvements program, giving Victorians more choice about how they travel on buses, and improving the connectivity of bus services to ongoing train and tram services.

Planning for the network changes will begin in early 2021, with timeframes for the changes to be communicated to the community in the coming months.

*All COVID Restrictions were adhered to in the filming of this video.

I’m interested - do you have experience working within Australian Disability Enterprises (ADEs)?

The ADE system was set up after successful lobbying by organisations (mostly non-profit and backed by religious institutions) as they stated employing people with disability (PWD) required extra support from staff, which impacted on their bottom line, due to having to pay for this from their own income stream. ADE participants are paid a % of the minimum wage, based upon their functional capacity; 50% capacity equals 50% minimum wage as your income. 

However, with the introduction of the NDIS in 2013, all this changed; ADE providers now receive funding from the NDIS to provide support to PWD within the ADE workplace. However, wages for PWD have not changed. 

One of my participant’s was offered $3.97 an hour for a 24 hour week - a quite physically and cognitively competent man. 

What is your experience? Do you think this is fair? To me, this is modern day slave labour. 

A fair days work equals a fair days wage. 

This is simply not good enough and it must be changed so PWD have a chance at earning a fair wage to improve their quality of life. 

Annastacia Palaszczuk Scott Morrison (ScoMo) NDIS National Disability Insurance SchemeBill Shorten Stuart Robert MP Queensland Human Rights Commission

Clive Palmer has today called for the resignation of WA Attorney General, John Quigley.

“It is the  WA’s chief law officer and barrister of the Supreme Court, John Quigley, that doesn’t support the rule of law and wishes to introduce unconstitutional legislation,” Mr Palmer said.

“Betrayal of the rule of law, exemptions from the criminal law and removing freedom of information is not what Australia is about.”

Mr Palmer said Mr Quigley was sponsoring a Bill into the WA Parliament which was both draconian and extraordinary. 

“It’s unsuitable to be the first legal officer of WA to do this. He has betrayed his duty. A case can be made that he is in contempt of the High Court of Australia,’’ Mr Palmer said.

“As well as seeking to destroy the rights of individuals and protect politicians from the criminal law, the Act also bans citizens taking to court any matter associated with the events and acts that caused the State to inflict substantial pain and damage. 

“No politician should be beyond public scrutiny and no politician should be both judge and executioner.

It feels like there is a pretty constant stream of bad news when it comes to climate change - and it can be completely disheartening to see the inaction and ineptitude of the Morrison Government on this issue.

Anna is CEO of ClimateWorks Australia and a founding director of the Clean Energy Finance Corporation. She says that regardless of what is happening at a federal level, an increasing number of businesses, state governments and other groups are working towards achieving net zero emissions by 2050 (or sooner).

We can also be optimistic about renewable energy technology getting better and better, and about all the benefits we’ll enjoy if we successfully transition to a low emissions economy. Farmers who are embracing climate action are already seeing the benefits in growing better quality fruit, and producing wool that is softer *and* stronger - how amazing is that?

How about you - are you optimistic about climate action in this country?

HOW DO YOU SUPER-CHARGE CHAPEL STREET?

<My response to emails wanting to know how I might improve Chapel Street>

There was a Chapel Street plan about 12 years ago which had some great ideas about how to improve it - and even back then described Chapel Street as lacking investment and run down. The execution of that master plan to date seems to have focused on Prahran Square, Windsor Station upgrades and a few other discrete areas but has not focused on the actual streets themselves - what they look like, feel like and what is actually there. 

I do not think that it is as simple as tidying up the streets, facades, removing the (bird/dog) poo and the gum and the grime - that is not enough in of itself to bring back businesses and customers (although it would be a nice start!) The reality is that retail has been struggling for a long time even before COVID, and COVID made the inevitable happen faster. (e.g. Think of the profound impact of online shopping and a lack of a consolidated vision for the area shared between landlords, council, businesses and residents.) The work that has been done to date (regardless of its expense) sits at the edges and is not enough to shock the street itself back to life. 

I think that Chapel Street needs a new vision. It will not be about making it what it was before because that time has passed. It needs to be a new offer for a new future and new needs by consumers and residents. We need to consider how Chapel St can be world-renowned and a place we are all immensely proud of once more. 

So there is no easy one answer. But the beginning of this process is about forming that vision and working in conjunction with landlords, tenants, residents, experts, and Council to make that happen. It would be arrogant for me to assume that I could know the answer to it all.... but I have a feeling that we will need to rethink the enjoyability of walking and cycling Chapel St (the more people walk or cycle, the more money they spend in retail), it may mean thinking more strategically about retail mix along the length of Chapel St, creating distinct and exciting zones along Chapel street that feel exciting in their own unique way (e.g. South Yarra vs Windsor), regular events that make it an exciting place people are drawn to, and even thinking about how the street evolves through the morning, day, evening and night so that it is nurtured to maximise the excitement and potential of the street through all ‘day-parts’. 

I have worked with brands like Melbourne Central (GPT) and Chadstone to help define and bring their brands to life... and worked with retail brands like Officeworks, Dan Murphy's, Kathmandu and McDonald's to innovate and evolve. I want to share that knowledge and experience with something closer to home that I deeply care about. 

=> These are just my thoughts, what do you think needs to be done?

Weed Update - Arundel Springs and The Wetlands

Meeting today in Arundel Springs with two of the Boffins (Paul and Lee) from 'Vector and Biosecurity' who gave me an update on the status of invasive plants on the ponds.

Always interesting when you get to meet with a couple of guys that spend their entire working time engrossed in the dietary plans and other behaviours of weevils.  You have to wonder what they talk about at parties.

However, the good news is that the Vector and Biosecurity team keeps a close eye on things in the wetlands, they love weevils and they love killing weeds.

I listened intently to their detailed information on Salvinia (bad plant) and Water Hyacinth (bad plant but with pretty purple flowers) and how they go about monitoring and controlling them.  

There is a fair bit there at the moment, but it’s not a disaster.  The team have dispatched a new squadron of purpose bred Weevils last weekend on their mission to clear the wetlands.  The results are starting to be visible (notice the contrast of brown - dead - and the green, not dead yet patches in photos). 

Unfortunately, the water bodies most affected by these pesky plants are all man made, and they assist greatly in the growth of these type of weeds. In addition, recent weather conditions have been perfect for weed growth, and not so perfect for weevil success.  In perfect conditions, weevils take some time to beat the Salvinia, but results are already starting to show.

They like to use biological means wherever possible, but at times will spot spray particularly troublesome areas and stubborn patches of Water Hyacinth (they also manually remove it).  Hopefully we get some rain in the near future, as this should assist greatly with the process of clearing the ponds.

Our May 5 vigil on the steps of Parliament House is aptly titled our “They Died Waiting Rally”, and is in memory of all those South Australians who’ve died waiting for legislation to pass since 1995. That’s when the very first Bill was introduced into the South Australian Parliament in a bid to bring voluntary assisted dying into law. Politicians are now debating the 17th Bill.

One of the many beautiful South Australians who wanted the right to choose, but died waiting, was Kylie Monaghan from Port Pirie. The brave 35-year-old was the face of the 2016 voluntary euthanasia campaign backed by Voluntary Assisted Dying South Australia and Andrew Denton’s Go Gentle Australia Foundation. Kylie was diagnosed with stage three breast cancer in 2010 and died in October 2016, but her powerful legacy in advocating for choice and compassion lives on.

With Upper House MPs set to resume debate on the Voluntary Assisted Dying Bill 2020 on the evening of May 5, please wear red and join us on the steps of Parliament House at midday in memory of those who’ve died waiting since 1996, and to show our politicians that the community wants this legislation passed now. No more delays. No more terminally ill South Australians who die in pain, waiting for the right to access voluntary assisted dying.

Today I spoke about Priya and Nades who came to Australia separately by boat in 2012 and 2013. They'd fled Sri Lanka because of persecution of the Tamils.  The couple married and settled in the Central Queensland town of Biloela, where they lived and worked. 

Their daughters, Kopika and Tharnicaa, were born in Australia. The family have been in detention on Christmas Island since August 2019—and Christmas Island, of course, is in my electorate.

On Tuesday this week the Federal Court stopped their deportation, upholding a decision made in April 2020, which the Department of Home Affairs has sought to have overturned. Labor welcomes the court's decision.  

In November 2019, whilst on Christmas Island as part of my regular visits, I met with this family and had the opportunity to witness their living circumstances and hear of what they had to say and about their situation. 

My plea to the Morrison Government is allow this family to stay. 

We don't need any more taxpayer money wasted keeping them in detention on Christmas Island, a family of four who pose no risk to the community.

At the very least, the minister should allow them the freedom of living in the community and, even better, allow them to return to Central Queensland, to the welcoming arms of the community of Biloela.

"HÃY HIẾN DÂNG TẤM THÂN NGỌC NGÀ CỦA CON 
CHO RIÊNG AI ĐÃ YÊU TÂM HỒN TRẦN TRỤI CỦA CON"
(Nguồn: https://www.facebook.com/thao.phanthanh.9)
.
Charlie Chapin - gần gũi hơn với khán giả Việt Nam qua tên "Vua Hề Sạc-Lô" - viết lá thư xúc động sau cho cô con gái cưng của mình đêm Giáng Sinh 1965.
.
****************
.
“Con gái của bố!

Bây giờ đang là đêm. Đêm Giáng Sinh. Các anh, chị của con đang ngủ. Mẹ con cũng đã ngủ rồi. Con ở xa bố biết bao! Nhưng hình ảnh con luôn luôn xuất hiện trước mắt bố. Chân dung con - ở đây, trên bàn, và ở đây, trong trái tim bố. Nơi ấy, thành Paris hoa lệ, con đang khiêu vũ trên sân khấu nhà hát hoành tráng của Điện Élysée. Bố biết rõ điều đó, nhưng dù sao bố cũng cảm thấy trong đêm khuya tĩnh lặng bố nghe được tiếng chân con bước, nhìn thấy cặp mắt con đang sáng lên như những vì sao trên bầu trời mùa đông.

Bố nghe nói rằng con sắm vai người đẹp Ba Tư bị một khan Tácta cầm tù trong vở kịch tưng bừng và vui tươi. Hãy làm người đẹp và hãy khiêu vũ! Nhưng nếu lòng mến mộ và biết ơn của công chúng mê hoặc con, nếu như hương thơm của những đóa hoa con được tặng làm đầu óc con choáng váng, thì hãy ngồi vào một góc kín và đọc bức thư của bố, hãy lắng nghe tiếng nói trái tim mình. Bố là bố của con, Geraldine ạ!

Bố là Charlie Chaplin! Con có biết bao nhiêu đêm bố đã ngồi bên giường con, khi con còn tấm bé, kể cho con nghe những câu chuyện cổ tích về người đẹp ngủ trong rừng, về con rồng nhiều phép lạ? Còn khi giấc ngủ làm díp đôi mắt già nua của bố, bố cười và nói: «Hãy đi đi! Giấc ngủ của ta – đó là ước mơ của con gái ta!".

Bố nhìn thấy những ước mơ của con, Geraldine ạ, nhìn thấy tương lai của con, ngày hôm nay của con.

Bố nhìn thấy một cô gái đang khiêu vũ trên sân khấu, một nàng tiên đang bay lượn trên bầu trời. Bố nghe thấy khán giả trầm trồ: “Có nhìn thấy cô gái ấy không? Cô ta là con gái của một anh hề già. Có biết ông ta là Charlie Chaplin không?”

Vâng, bố là Chaplin! Bố là một anh hề già! Hôm nay đến lượt con. Hãy khiêu vũ! Bố đã mặc chiếc quần rách rộng thùng thình để khiêu vũ, còn con mặc tấm áo lụa dài của một công chúa để khiêu vũ. Những vũ điệu này và những tiếng vỗ tay như sấm dậy có lúc sẽ nâng con lên chín tầng mây. Con hãy bay! Hãy bay tới đó. Nhưng con cũng hãy hạ cánh xuống mặt đất! Con phải nhìn thấy cuộc sống của những con người, cuộc sống của những vũ công đường phố đang vừa nhảy vừa run lên vì lạnh và đói.

Bố đã từng như vậy, như họ, Geraldine ạ. Vào những đêm ấy, những đêm kỳ diệu, khi con chìm vào giấc ngủ bởi những câu chuyện cổ tích của bố, bố vẫn không hề chợp mắt.

Bố nhìn gương mặt bé xíu của con, lắng nghe nhịp tim con đập và tự hỏi: “Này, Charlie, phải chăng con mèo con này một lúc nào đó sẽ nhận ra ngươi?” Con chưa hiểu hiểu hết bố đâu, Geraldine ạ. Bố đã kể cho con nghe nhiều chuyện cổ tích vào những đêm xa xưa ấy, nhưng chưa bao giờ kể cho con nghe chuyện cổ tích của mình. Mà nó cũng rất lý thú. Đó là câu chuyện cổ tích về một anh hề đói đã hát và nhảy trong những khu phố nghèo của London, và sau đó đi xin bố thí. Đó là chuyện cổ tích của bố! Bố biết thế nào là cái đói, thế nào là không chốn nương thân. Hơn nữa, bố đã nếm trải nỗi khổ nhục của một anh hề rong, trong ngực sục sôi một đại dương kiêu hãnh, và niềm kiêu hãnh này bị tổn thương bởi những đồng xu người ta ném cho bố. Nhưng dù sao bố vẫn sống, vì vậy hãy bỏ qua điều đó.

Tốt nhất là hãy nói về con. Sau tên con - Geraldine - là họ của bố - Chaplin. Với cái họ này hơn 40 năm bố đã mua vui cho mọi người trên trái đất. Nhưng bố khóc nhiều hơn họ cười. Geraldine ạ, trong thế giới con đang sống không chỉ có vũ điệu và âm nhạc! Đêm đêm, khi bước ra từ khán phòng lớn, con có thể quên những người hâm mộ giàu sang, nhưng đừng quên hỏi thăm vợ người tài xế taxi chở con về nhà. Và nếu như cô ta đang mang bầu, nếu như họ không có tiền để sắm tã lót cho đứa con tương lai, con hãy đặt tiền vào túi anh ta. Bố đã đề nghị nhà băng thanh toán các khoản chi phí của con. Nhưng những món nợ của những người khác con cũng phải trả đầy đủ. Thỉnh thoảng con nên đi tàu điện ngầm hay ôtô buýt, đi bộ để ngắm thành phố.

Hãy quan tâm tới mọi người! Hãy để ý tới những góa phụ và trẻ em mồ côi! Và ít ra là một lần trong ngày, con hãy tự nói với mình: “Mình cũng giống họ thôi”. Vâng, con cũng là một trong số họ, con gái ạ. Hơn nữa. Nghệ thuật, trước khi cho con người ta đôi cánh để có thể bay cao, thường bẻ gãy chân anh ta. Và nếu như có một ngày con cảm thấy mình cao hơn công chúng, thì ngay lập tức hãy bỏ sân khấu. Con hãy bắt chiếc taxi đầu tiên và đi ra ngoại ô Paris. Bố biết rất rõ những vùng này. Ở đấy con sẽ nhìn thấy nhiều vũ nữ giống như con, thậm chí xinh đẹp hơn, duyên dáng hơn, với niềm kiêu hãnh lớn. Ở đấy không ai biết tới ánh đèn sân khấu rực rỡ của con. 

Đối với họ đèn sân khấu là mặt Trăng.

Con hãy nhìn thật kỹ! Có phải họ khiêu vũ tốt hơn con không? Hãy thừa nhận đi, con yêu! Bao giờ cũng có thể tìm thấy người khiêu vũ đẹp hơn con, diễn hay hơn con.

Và hãy ghi nhớ: trong gia đình Charlie không có kẻ thô lỗ có thể mắng chửi người xà ích hay giễu cợt kẻ hành khất đang ngồi bên bờ sông Seine. Bố sẽ chết, nhưng con sẽ sống. Bố muốn con không bao giờ biết đến sự nghèo khổ. Cùng với bức thư này bố chuyển cho con một cuốn séc để con có thể chi tiêu tùy thích. Nhưng khi con tiêu 2 phrăng, đừng quên nhắc nhở mình rằng đồng phrăng thứ ba không phải của con. Nó phải thuộc về một người lạ mặt đang cần đến nó. Mà người đó con có thể dễ dàng tìm thấy. Chỉ cần con muốn nhìn thấy những người lạ mặt nghèo khổ là con sẽ gặp họ khắp nơi. Bố nói với con về tiền, vì bố biết được sức mạnh khủng khiếp của nó.

Bố đã làm việc khá lâu trong rạp xiếc. Và bao giờ bố cũng rất lo lắng cho những người đi trên dây. Nhưng phải nói với con rằng con người hay bị vấp ngã trên mặt đất hơn trên sợi dây mạo hiểm. Có thể, vào một trong những buổi dạ hội mà con được mời, ánh sáng của một viên kim cương nào đấy sẽ làm con lóa mắt. Đúng lúc đó, nó sẽ là sợi dây thừng mạo hiểm đối với con, và con không thể tránh được sự vấp ngã. Có thể, vào một ngày đẹp trời, gương mặt tuyệt mỹ của một hoàng tử nào đó sẽ hút hồn con. Chính vào cái ngày hôm ấy, con sẽ trở thành một người đi trên dây thiếu kinh nghiệm, mà những người thiếu kinh nghiệm bao giờ cũng dễ vấp ngã. Con đừng bán trái tim mình vì vàng bạc, châu báu.
--
Hãy nhớ rằng viên kim cương lớn nhất của con là mặt trời. 

May mắn thay, nó tỏa sáng cho tất cả mọi người. Còn đến một lúc nào đó, con bắt đầu yêu, thì hãy yêu thương con người đó với tất cả trái tim. Bố đã nói với mẹ viết cho con về điều đó. Trong tình yêu, mẹ hiểu biết nhiều hơn bố, tốt nhất là để mẹ nói với con. Công việc của con đầy khó khăn, bố biết điều đó.

Thân thể con chỉ được che bằng một mảnh lụa. Vì nghệ thuật có thể xuất hiện thoát y trên sân khấu, nhưng phải trở về từ đó không những trong y phục mà còn sạch sẽ hơn.

Bố đã già, và có thể, lời bố nói nghe buồn cười. Nhưng, theo bố, thân thể thoát y của con phải thuộc về kẻ nào yêu tâm hồn cởi mở của con. Không có gì đáng sợ nếu như đây là ý kiến 10 năm trước của con về vấn đề này, nghĩa là nó thuộc về quá khứ. Đừng sợ, 10 năm không làm con già đi. Bố biết rằng giữa thế hệ bố và con luôn luôn có sự đối đầu. Con hãy quyết đấu với bố, với ý nghĩ của bố. Bố không thích những đứa con dễ bảo. Và khi mà nước mắt của bố chưa rỏ xuống bức thư này, bố muốn tin rằng Giáng Sinh hôm nay là một đêm kỳ diệu.

Bố muốn điều kỳ diệu sẽ xảy ra, và con thực sự hiểu tất cả những gì bố muốn nói với con. Bố Charlie đã già thật rồi, con gái Geraldine ạ. Sớm hay muộn, thay cho chiếc áo dài trắng dành cho sân khấu con phải mặc bộ áo tang để bước tới nấm mồ của bố. Bây giờ bố không muốn làm con buồn. Có điều thỉnh thoảng con nên soi gương - trong đấy con sẽ nhìn thấy những đường nét của bố. Trong huyết quản của con đang chảy dòng máu của bố. Ngay cả khi máu trong huyết quản bố đã khô cạn, bố vẫn muốn con không quên bố Charlie của mình. Bố không phải là thiên thần, nhưng luôn luôn khao khát trở thành một con người. 

Cố gắng lên, con nhé!
Hôn con, Geraldine, 

Charlie của con.

The West Australian government has committed $1.8 billion to build a new women’s and babies hospital to replace the ageing King Edward Memorial Hospital. While I fully support the development of a new purpose built hospital I do have concerns regarding some of the detail, especially the proposed location. 
The government’s proposal is for the new hospital to be built at the Queen Elizabeth II  Medical Centre. This will allow the sale of what the government refers to as a “very valuable piece of real estate”.

The relocation of another large-scale medical service to the QE2 site must raise alarm bells. This site is already extremely congested since the relocation of the children’s hospital to the site. We currently have a situation which sees some nurses having to arrive at work up to an hour prior to the commencement of the shift just to gain entry and obtain parking. Thomas Street which runs adjacent to the hospital is already congested and resembles a carpark more than a major road during peak hour which also coincides with the hospitals change of shift. Thomas road also caters for staff and visitors attending the adjacent Hollywood Hospital and numerous specialty suites that all add to traffic congestion.

While I understand the benefit of putting health services in a central location to allow them to share services and resources, the location must ultimately be user friendly. Supportive infrastructure including public transport must be a priority in the decision making process. Lack of planning in this area only benefits the privately owned car park operators.

Let’s create an active transport boom and meet our modal share targets.
We make around 700,000 trips a day in Moreland. 
Approx. 420,000 to 450,000 are made with a car. That’s around 60 to 65%.
If we want to compete with the future progressive cities of the world and have an effective, safe and sustainable transport network we have to get car trips down to 20%. 
For now though, let’s go for a target of 40%, which is the Moreland Integrated Transport Strategy’s target area and about as much as a local council can do without State government support.
That’s a reduction of approx. 155,000 car trips a day in Moreland and therefore an additional 155,000 trips by foot or bike per day. 
The car trips we have to focus on are the short trips to our local destinations: our schools, shops, parks, tram stops and train stations. We do around 200,000 of these every day.
Replacing 155,000 car trips a day in Moreland with trips by foot or bike is a great target to aim for and one we can achieve over the next 10 years but in order to meet that target, I believe we’ll need to do the following things.
1. Make active transport a bigger priority in Moreland’s budget and look for a new revenue source to fund an expanded 10-year cycling plan that connects all of our schools, shops, parks and train stations to a network of separated bike lanes and off-road shared paths. 
2. Implement Moreland’s Integrated Transport Strategy’s aim to make our local roads safer for walking and cycling by preventing drivers from using local roads for short cuts. 
3. Reduce speed limits on local roads to 30km/h and promote these local roads as the walking connections to our local destinations.
4. Look into developers providing land contributions instead of cash contributions with the intention of creating new active transport corridors when large parcels of land are being developed. 
5. Convert 25% of all Moreland City Council owned car parks into open space and include active transport connections where there are destinations to link on either end of the new space. This small reduction on our oversupply of car spaces will only inconvenience short car trips of up to about 400 metres to these destinations. People making these journeys by car will eventually switch those short trips to mostly walking and a little bit of cycling. My name is Justin Turner and I am running not only for the North West Ward in the upcoming Frankston City Council elections for 2020, but for change.

Before diving into some key policy aims a little bit of background about me. I am a local Frankston North resident, ratepayer and business owner in our city. I live, work, send my sons to school here and as a part of my vocation, I am in constant communication at a grass roots level with owners, residents and businesses. I’ve (in the past) been heavily involved with another city council, not so dissimilar to Frankston that was forward thinking and focused on community engagement and it’s successful management was enforced by many other municipalities. I was one of the first members of the youth task force model; that has shown success across many shires nationally, where adopted; to include youth participation on a range of issues and services to give council an insight and real input into making the city a better place for our future. 

As someone that invests into our community in both business and personal, along with a unique insight into how we can efficiently change how we run our city to cut costs, improve services and build a city that future generations will be proud to live in, without losing our identity. 

Some key aims when I am elected as your voice:

1. Change to our ever increasing rates, particularly during a recession and in time’s where ever single person in our city are doing it tough.  As a council and as a city we need to ensure that we are fiscal with our income and not frivolously wasting funds. I will spearhead community consultation into where we as a community need to focus our funds into. Review services in place including upcoming tenders to ensure value for money and to bring a spotlight of transparency for the general public. Find allocation evenly throughout each suburb for public spaces to ensure that each suburb is invested into and has their own sense of identity and a draw card to residents now and into the future. 

2. Review dilapidated and disused assets and form a feasibility on continual maintenance/upkeep or disposal. Whilst it’s important to point out that any loss of a public space is far from ideal, if it’s beyond economical and community benefit, the revenue raised can offset the rates or perhaps be reused for another purpose within the community.

3. Broader Community Consultation, by reviewing what we have in place and forming new groups that adequately represent our community from geographic to demographic. This will ensure as your council we are working with you on matters that matter to you. I will form the foundation of a youth task force to have young people’s input into the governance of our city on a proactive and involved role without any tokenism.

4. A 20 year plan, which I am pleased that the council have now raised. My 20 year keystone envisions a footprint on how Frankston will look over the next 20 years, in terms of services, development and zoning. We need to identify now, what areas are going to be high density including environmental impact and development contribution to upgrades where appropriate. Ensuring we have consistent zoning inline with this plan. Furthermore I support reviewing the Carrum Downs business/commercial hub to centralise heavy commercial, allow for growth including job growth and wealth creation. 

5. Incentives for our CBD to encourage rent reductions, in turn bringing business back into Frankston and fostering potential for local new businesses and naturally Job creation.

6. And a focus on getting the 3 Rs right. Roads, Rates & Rubbish.

These are some key criteria I will focus on that I believe we as a city need to change, that we need to make better. A vote for me, is a vote for one of your peers, I am contactable and believe that Frankston has so much more potential to be an absolute gateway to the peninsular, but we need to get our basics right first, engage with each and every one of you and not only rely on the same groups we’ve always had. 

In closing, I don’t claim to know alll the answers or have a solution to everything. I do however, have an unwavering commitment to you, my family and our businesses to make our city an amazing place to visit, live and work. A vote for me is a vote for your future. 

Call me if I can help and if you have any issues to raise 0468 44 55 44.

BREAKING! Christian Charity Barnabas Calls on Prime Minister Scott Morrison to Recognise the Armenian Genocide

Christian charity, Barnabas Fund has joined growing calls on Prime Minister Scott Morrison to recognise the Armenian Genocide, and initiated a petition that is being distributed through their network churches across the country, reported the Armenian National Committee of Australia (ANC-AU).

Barnabas Fund Australia is the local branch of a global organisation that is most well known for defending the human rights of persecuted and discriminated Christians through the provision of aid and by speaking out against the persecution of Christian minorities.

During meetings with the Armenian National Committee of Australia and the Armenian Missionary Association of Australia, Barnabas Fund Australia CEO Ashley Saunders revealed details of the global petition campaign from their organisation, which was calling on the United States, United Kingdom, Israel, New Zealand and Australia to recognise the systematic attempt to rid the world of the Armenians, Assyrians and Greeks as genocide.

The Australian version of the petition calls upon the Australian Government to “officially recognise as genocide the mass murder of Armenian, Assyrian, Syriac and Greek Christians in the Ottoman Empire before, during and after the first world war”.

ANC-AU has welcomed the solidarity of Barnabas Fund Australia, as pressure increases on the Australian Government in the lead-up to the 106th Anniversary of the Armenian Genocide.

“We applaud Barnabas Fund Australia for taking on this great initiative by calling on the Australian Government to join over 30 nations across the international community in recognising the 1915 Genocide the Armenians, Assyrians and Greeks,” said ANC-AU Executive Director Haig Kayserian.

Kayserian added: “We encourage all allies of justice to sign this petition and join our calls on Scott Morrison’s Government to recognise the Armenian Genocide.”

The Armenian National Committee of Australia wrote to Prime Minister Scott Morrison earlier this month, requesting his statement on the occasion of the 106th Anniversary of the Armenian Genocide to accurately characterise the occasion.

Over the past two weeks I have been asked by Members of the Education Party of Western Australia about the state of EPWA and I have been reluctant to decide its future. 

Last weekend, this changed. I walked into Charlies to purchase some cakes for my Grandfather and Grandmother. I was served by a former student and I happily greeted him and was surprised when he reached over the counter and shook my hand. He told me that he never had the opportunity to say that I was the first person to help him in this country and that I had a dramatic impact on his life. It was such a raw and beautiful moment. After shaking his hand too many times, I left Charlies with a somewhat teary smile that turned to introspection. It came to me that I am not a teacher anymore, that these moments will never arise again and this birthed a confliction of emotions that caused me to reflect on EPWA and the questions about the state of EPWA.

I started this Party for students like the one who shook my hand, to help teachers like me not leave the profession, to challenge the Unions to do more, to be a catalyst to form a path to a new and relevant curriculum and fight to clear the stagnation in the bureaucracy. Although these are lofty ambitions, the initial steps of the Party were brilliant and purposeful. EPWA’s most recent forays, however, have been tiptoes… the Party has been markedly absent. 

The honest reason is that I stopped driving it. I resigned from teaching last year because I lost my belief in the system that I worked in. I believed the actions of my principal in dealing with a colleague to be so out of kilter with the ethics that CEWA purports to represent that I decided that I had to put my feet where my mouth was. I created this Party to fight for people like my colleague and I walked the walk and called out the principal for what I perceived were gross injustices and I am proud of what I did. I never expected the emotional fallout to be so overwhelming. Not only did I leave students that I cared dearly about, the two sport teams that I coached, my afterschool Film Society but at the same time a malicious and hurtful lie about the death of my father surfaced from a colleague that I helped numerous times. 

The actions of CEWA and the principal, the lack of support I received, the fallacies about my late father, and the reasliation that I could have acted to protect my colleague in a much more effective and mature way conflated into a barrier I could not traverse. I had not only lost faith in the system I trusted, I lost my faith in the people that I sought to uplift and support and, embarrassingly, I lost faith in myself.

The following months saw little action in EPWA and although I promised that in the new year I would set goals to bring to light CEWA’s inaction, to encourage the SSTUWA to be more active, to push for more members, host more meetings, my drive had vanished with my fortitude and my mental health. 

I am not ashamed to say that but, nonetheless, it hurts. 

In such light, the only answer to the question “What of EPWA now?” is that EPWA must remain dormant for the election, remain unregistered, and for a duration after. Although this is a difficult decision, we will find new direction and new leadership in the time to come. 

Ultimately, my failure as a leader, as a teacher, my failure in maintaining my mental health and in protecting my colleague and friend matters little now. 

All that matters is that teachers are supported so that a thousand teachers can enter a thousand local shops, bump into past students and for those students to shake their hands and say…
You made a difference. 

That is what really matters. 
Luke Stewart. 
Party President.

Cuối cùng khi cả đoàn được phép ra sân bay, họ ra lịnh cấm chúng tôi không được cười giỡn, chuyện trò và tuyệt đối cấm không được chụp hình. Họ càng cấm thì tôi càng quạu và đã lén chụp được một tấm hình tại đây để làm kỷ niệm. Tấm hình độc nhất tại Đông Bá Linh sau này được nhiều người trong phái đoàn xin sang lại.

Cảm giác tù túng, mất tự do xuyên suốt chuyến đi từ Đông Bá Linh sang Leningrad, rồi trở về, đã luôn theo đuổi tôi.

Tại sao những người Đông Âu thông minh trí thức mà tôi có dịp gặp gỡ chuyện trò, lại có thể tiếp tay xây dựng một chế độ độc tài tàn bạo như vậy? 

Tại sao họ bằng lòng giam hãm mình trong một nhà tù khổng lồ, chấp nhận một đời sống hẩm hiu như súc vật?
.

BỨC TƯỜNG BÁ LINH

Khỏi cần nói cũng hiểu tôi vui mừng biết bao khi thấy bức tường Bá Linh sụp đổ. Tôi vui như thể Việt Nam được giải phóng. Tôi khâm phục khả năng lãnh đạo của Chancellor Helmut Kohl. Nhờ biết nắm bắt thời cơ, nhờ tài thương lượng tuyệt vời, ông đã cứu người dân Đông Đức ra khỏi nanh vuốt cộng sản, dẫu phải chuộc sự tự do của họ bằng một số tiền khủng là 16 tỉ mark.

Với công trình thống nhất đất nước rất ngoạn mục không tốn một giọt máu nào, tôi đinh ninh người dân hai miền Đông và Tây Đức sẽ biết ơn ông Kohl suốt đời.
.

ĐỜI KHÔNG NHƯ LÀ MƠ!

Quả thật, đời không như là mơ. Chỉ chưa đầy hai năm sau, niềm hoan hỉ tột cùng đã nhường chỗ cho một sự thật cay đắng phũ phàng.

Người Đông Đức (ĐĐ) đã nhận ra chỉ trên dưới 30 năm sinh sống dưới chế độ Cộng sản, họ đã thua sút Tây Đức (TĐ) quá xa về mọi mặt. Từ vật chất đến tinh thần. Từ phong cách sống đến thái độ làm việc. Nhưng sâu thẳm nhất là sự thua sút về mặt tư tưởng.

Người ĐĐ thấy mình nghèo khó hơn người TĐ nên đâm ra ganh tị. Bản chất thụ động làm cho họ có thói quen ngồi trông chờ một lãnh tụ anh minh mơ hồ nào đó ban phát bổng lộc. Họ quen sống lươn lẹo dối trá mánh mun hối lộ để được việc. Khi không thành công trong một xã hội văn minh, dân chủ và nhân bản, họ thất vọng ê chề nên đổ lỗi ngược lại cho những người TĐ giàu sang là kỳ thị, không biết tôn trọng di sản 'văn hóa cộng sản' của họ.
.

BESSERWESSI VÀ JAMMEROSSI

Người TĐ ngỡ ngàng. 

Những tưởng tiền thuế lao động của mình dùng để thống nhất đất nước, chuộc lấy sự tự do cho những người cùng quê hương ra khỏi ngục tù cộng sản là một hành động thiêng liêng cao cả. Nhưng không!

Có nhiều người ĐĐ buông ra những câu nói cực kỳ vô ơn: ''Biết vậy thà để chúng tôi sống với Cộng sản còn có lý hơn!'' "Chúng tôi còn có công ăn việc làm, mặc dầu phải làm những công việc vô nghĩa''. Vì kiến thức lỗi thời, làm việc không hữu hiệu, thiếu trách nhiệm, cộng thêm tâm lý bệnh hoạn nên ít hãng xưởng, công ty nào dám nhận họ vào.  Người TĐ lâm vào cảnh 'làm ơn mắc oán'.

Hai từ tiếng Đức đặt biệt ra đời trong thời gian này thể hiện một quốc gia, hai thái cực, là 'Jammerossi' và 'Besserwessi'.

Người TĐ gọi người ĐĐ là ''Jammerossi'', những người luôn ăn vạ, than vãn, không có tinh thần cầu tiến. ''Besserwessi'' là từ người ĐĐ chửi những người TĐ cao ngạo, cái gì cũng nghĩ mình biết rành rẽ hơn. Niềm vui thống nhất của Đông và Tây Đức do đó đã nguội dần sau một thời gian ngắn.

30 năm, sau khi bức tường Bá Linh kiên cố sụp đổ, bức tường vô hình giữa Ossi (Đông) và Wessi (Tây) vẫn chưa san bằng được. Thậm chí càng ngày nó càng có vẻ kiên cố hơn. Người dân dần dà chấp nhận: 'Sẽ không có một biện pháp hòa giải nào thích đáng giữa Đông và Tây trong tương lai gần nhất'.

Tôi cũng hết vô tư ăn mừng giải phóng. Thay vào đó, tôi tìm đến ngành tâm lý xã hội, hy vọng mình có thể giải đáp một câu hỏi:

''Tại sao Bức Tường Bá Linh Ô Nhục bằng gạch, bằng sắt, dầy đặc hàng rào kẽm gai, lại có thể sụp đổ dễ dàng trong một đêm? Trong khi 80 triệu bức tường Bá Linh vô hình kia vẫn còn tồn tại được suốt hơn nửa thế kỷ?'

Lữ Thị Tường Uyên
Thứ Hai, 11-11-2019

Teachers' salaries will be made equal to their level of training and responsibility.

#savethemanlyferries

15.1 NOTICE OF MOTION NO 44/2020 - SAVE THE LARGE MANLY FERRIES

286/20 RESOLVED
Cr Bingham / Cr Sprott

That:

1. Council make representations to the relevant authorities to delay the State Government’s decision to retire the 1100 passenger capacity Freshwater-class ferries and to replace them with 400 passenger capacity Emerald-class ferries, commencing next year.

A. Council arrange urgent meetings with the Minister for Transport, the Hon Andrew Constance MP, and the Chief Operations Officer of Transport for NSW, Howard Collins; the Minister for Tourism, the Hon Stuart Ayres MP and Member for Manly, James Griffin MP.

B. Council seek assurances that required ferry passenger demand will continue to be met.

C. Council seek information from the State Government regarding the environmental impacts of the proposed changes.

2. While it is acknowledged that the existing old ferries are in need of maintenance and repair, Council is seeking assurances that the necessary repairs will be carried out, allowing time for a Fleet Replacement Plan to be developed which includes double-ended vessels with a 1000+ passenger capacity.

3. An impact assessment be prepared in consultation with the Manly Business Chamber, outlining the financial, brand and heritage impacts to Manly and Sydney’s visitor/tourist economy should the large ferries no longer be part of this route.

4. The resolution is to be sent by the CEO to:

A. The Legislative Assembly Committee on Transport and Infrastructure, Chaired by Robyn Preston MP, Member for Hawkesbury.

B. The Legislative Council Portfolio Committee No. 6 – Transport and Customer Service, Chaired by the Hon Abigail Boyd MLC.
